questions.stem: A 29-year-old woman reports increased vaginal discharge with a fishy odor that is most noticeable after intercourse, along with mild irritation. Speculum examination shows a thin, gray, homogeneous discharge adhering to the vaginal walls; the cervix appears normal. Vaginal pH is 5.2. Which of the following is most likely to be seen on saline wet mount of the discharge?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Budding yeast forms with pseudohyphae

choices.label: B
choices.text: Epithelial cells coated with adherent bacteria

choices.label: C
choices.text: Pear-shaped motile flagellated protozoa

choices.label: D
choices.text: Sheets of neutrophils among inflamed cells

choices.label: E
choices.text: Uniformly pale, translucent squamous cells only

explanation.summary: Clue cells (squamous epithelial cells coated with bacteria) are the characteristic microscopic finding of bacterial vaginosis.
explanation.whyCorrect: Thin gray homogeneous discharge, fishy odor worse after sex, a normal cervix, and pH above 4.5 point to bacterial vaginosis. Its characteristic wet-mount finding is the clue cell: a vaginal squamous epithelial cell with bacteria adhering to its surface, one of the four Amsel criteria.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Budding yeast with pseudohyphae indicate vaginal candidiasis, which has a thick 'cottage cheese' discharge, minimal odor, and a normal pH of 4.0-4.5.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Flagellated pyriform protozoa indicate trichomoniasis, which causes a frothy yellow-green discharge and may produce a strawberry cervix.
whyWrongByChoice.D: BV is a vaginosis, not a true 'itis': there is little inflammation and no white cells. Neutrophil-rich inflammation fits trichomoniasis.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Uniformly pale, translucent squamous cells are the normal appearance; this patient meets several Amsel criteria for BV, so clue cells are expected.

questions.stem: A 24-year-old woman has 4 days of intense vulvar itching and burning with urination. Examination shows erythema and edema of the vulva and vaginal mucosa with a thick, white, clumped discharge that has minimal odor. The cervix appears normal. Vaginal pH is 4.2. Which of the following is most likely to be seen on microscopy of the discharge?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Budding yeast with pseudohyphae

choices.label: B
choices.text: Lemon-shaped cells with four flagella

choices.label: C
choices.text: Pale squamous cells without organisms

choices.label: D
choices.text: Sheets of gram-variable coccobacilli

choices.label: E
choices.text: Squamous cells studded with coccobacilli

explanation.summary: Vulvovaginal candidiasis shows budding yeast and pseudohyphae on microscopy.
explanation.whyCorrect: Pruritus, vulvovaginal erythema and edema, a thick 'cottage cheese' discharge with little odor, a normal cervix, and a normal pH (4.0-4.5) are the classic picture of vaginal candidiasis. The classic microscopy finding is budding yeast with pseudohyphae.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Lemon-shaped flagellated protozoa indicate trichomoniasis, which raises pH above 4.5 and causes a frothy yellow-green malodorous discharge.
whyWrongByChoice.C: This patient is clearly symptomatic with inflammatory findings; microscopy is expected to show the causative yeast.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Gram-variable coccobacilli describe Gardnerella vaginalis of bacterial vaginosis, which does not produce marked erythema or a normal pH.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Clue cells (squamous cells coated with bacteria) indicate bacterial vaginosis, which has a pH above 4.5, a thin gray discharge, and a fishy odor.

questions.stem: A 22-year-old woman with several new sexual partners and inconsistent condom use has a frothy, yellow-green, malodorous vaginal discharge with vaginal soreness that worsens during intercourse. Vaginal pH is 6.0. Which of the following best describes the most likely causative organism?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Cyst-forming protozoan transmitted mainly by the fecal-oral route

choices.label: B
choices.text: Gram-negative diplococcus that infects the endocervical canal

choices.label: C
choices.text: Gram-variable coccobacillus that thrives as lactobacilli decline

choices.label: D
choices.text: Lemon-shaped protozoan with a single nucleus and four flagella

choices.label: E
choices.text: Opportunistic yeast that forms germ tubes when placed in serum

explanation.summary: Trichomonas vaginalis is a lemon-shaped, highly motile protozoan with a single nucleus, an undulating membrane, and four flagella at one end.
explanation.whyCorrect: A frothy yellow-green malodorous discharge, pH above 4.5, and high-risk sexual behavior indicate trichomoniasis. T. vaginalis is a protozoan that is lemon (pear) shaped, has a single nucleus and an undulating membrane, and is highly motile with four flagella at one end.

whyWrongByChoice.A: T. vaginalis lacks a cyst form, which is why it is transmitted essentially only through sexual contact.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Neisseria gonorrhoeae causes cervicitis and must be ruled out in vaginitis, but the frothy yellow-green discharge with high pH is the picture of trichomoniasis.
whyWrongByChoice.C: This describes Gardnerella vaginalis, the main organism of bacterial vaginosis, which causes a thin gray discharge with a fishy odor rather than a frothy yellow-green one.
whyWrongByChoice.E: This describes Candida, which produces a thick white discharge with minimal odor and a normal vaginal pH.

questions.stem: A 26-year-old woman is diagnosed with trichomoniasis by nucleic acid amplification testing. She has one male sexual partner, who has no symptoms. Which of the following is the most appropriate management?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Metronidazole vaginal gel for her; no treatment for her partner

choices.label: B
choices.text: Oral metronidazole for both of them and a pause in sexual activity

choices.label: C
choices.text: Oral metronidazole for her; treat her partner only if symptomatic

choices.label: D
choices.text: Single-dose oral fluconazole for both of them and condom use

choices.label: E
choices.text: Topical clotrimazole for her and condom use with her partner

explanation.summary: Trichomoniasis is treated with oral metronidazole, the partner is treated too, and sexual activity is paused until the infection clears.
explanation.whyCorrect: Metronidazole is the drug of choice for T. vaginalis, and the oral route is always preferred. Because the organism is sexually transmitted and colonizes the male urethra and prostate (usually without symptoms in men), the partner is also treated, and sex should be paused until the infection has cleared.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Topical metronidazole is ineffective for trichomoniasis because the organism lives in the urethra and perivaginal glands, and the partner must also be treated.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Male infection is typically asymptomatic, so waiting for symptoms would leave a reservoir for reinfection; the partner is treated regardless.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Fluconazole is an azole antifungal for candidiasis and has no role against a protozoan.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Clotrimazole is a topical antifungal for mild candidiasis and does not treat T. vaginalis.

questions.stem: A 31-year-old woman who douches daily and recently completed a course of antibiotics is diagnosed with bacterial vaginosis. Her vaginal pH is 5.4. Which of the following sequences best explains the rise in her vaginal pH?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Candida overgrowth consumes glycogen and depletes vaginal acid

choices.label: B
choices.text: Fewer lactobacilli make less lactic acid, and anaerobes flourish

choices.label: C
choices.text: Increased lactobacilli ferment sugars into alkaline by-products

choices.label: D
choices.text: Neutrophil influx releases alkaline granules into vaginal fluid

choices.label: E
choices.text: Trichomonad cytotoxins destroy epithelium and liberate base

explanation.summary: In BV, loss of lactobacilli reduces lactic acid, raising pH above 4.5, which in turn favors anaerobic overgrowth.
explanation.whyCorrect: Healthy vaginal lactobacilli metabolize sugars to lactic acid, keeping pH below 4.5 and protecting against anaerobes. Douching and antibiotics disrupt this microbiota; lactobacilli decline, lactic acid production falls, pH rises, and the higher pH promotes further anaerobic growth.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Candida does not deplete lactobacilli, and vaginal candidiasis keeps a normal pH of 4.0-4.5.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Lactobacilli produce lactic acid, which acidifies the vagina; BV is marked by a decrease in lactobacilli, not an increase.
whyWrongByChoice.D: BV has little inflammation and no white cells, so neutrophil products cannot explain the pH change.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Cytotoxic epithelial damage is the mechanism of trichomoniasis, not bacterial vaginosis.

questions.stem: A 17-year-old girl who has never been sexually active is diagnosed with bacterial vaginosis. Her mother, who accompanies her, is upset and asks whether the diagnosis means her daughter has been having sex. Which of the following is the most accurate response?

choices.label: A
choices.text: BV develops only after intercourse exposes the vagina to semen

choices.label: B
choices.text: BV follows ascending spread from an untreated cervicitis

choices.label: C
choices.text: BV is sexually transmitted, so she must have had a partner

choices.label: D
choices.text: BV reflects a flora imbalance and can occur without sex

choices.label: E
choices.text: BV results from yeast invading the vaginal epithelium

explanation.summary: Bacterial vaginosis is a flora imbalance, not an STI, and can develop in people who are abstinent.
explanation.whyCorrect: BV results from loss of microbial balance: lactobacilli decline and anaerobes overgrow. Sexual practices contribute to risk, but many other activities (douching, antibiotics, intravaginal products) can cause it, and abstinent people can develop BV. Of the three main causes of vaginitis, only trichomoniasis is a true STI.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Semen exposure can worsen odor and sex is a risk factor, but BV can develop without any sexual activity.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Untreated STIs can ascend and cause PID; BV is a vaginal flora disorder, not a consequence of cervicitis.
whyWrongByChoice.C: BV is not considered an STI; only trichomoniasis among the three main causes of vaginitis is.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Yeast invasion of tissue describes vaginal candidiasis, not bacterial vaginosis.

questions.stem: A 30-year-old woman with uncomplicated vulvovaginal candidiasis is treated with a single oral dose of fluconazole, and her symptoms resolve. Which of the following is the mechanism of action of this drug?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Blocks peptidoglycan cross-linking in the cell wall

choices.label: B
choices.text: Disables the undulating membrane that drives motility

choices.label: C
choices.text: Forms free radicals that fragment intracellular DNA

choices.label: D
choices.text: Inhibits ergosterol synthesis for the fungal cell membrane

choices.label: E
choices.text: Restores lactobacilli that ferment sugar into lactic acid

explanation.summary: Azole antifungals such as fluconazole act by inhibiting ergosterol synthesis.
explanation.whyCorrect: The main antifungal class used for vaginal candidiasis is the azoles, which inhibit ergosterol synthesis. A one-time oral dose of fluconazole is typically effective.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Peptidoglycan is a bacterial cell-wall component; it is not the azole target and is absent from fungi.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The undulating membrane belongs to T. vaginalis, a protozoan that is not treated with fluconazole.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Free-radical formation that destroys DNA is the mechanism of metronidazole, used for BV and trichomoniasis.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Azoles act directly on the fungus; candidiasis is not a lactobacillus-deficient state.

questions.stem: A 28-year-old woman was treated at an urgent care center with metronidazole vaginal gel for trichomoniasis. Three weeks later she still has a malodorous discharge and repeat testing remains positive for Trichomonas vaginalis. Her only partner completed oral therapy, and they have abstained since. Which of the following best explains her treatment failure?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Metronidazole has no activity against protozoal parasites

choices.label: B
choices.text: The gel raised vaginal pH above the drug's active range

choices.label: C
choices.text: The organism forms dormant cysts that resist metronidazole

choices.label: D
choices.text: The organism is a yeast that requires an azole antifungal

choices.label: E
choices.text: The organism persists in the urethra and perivaginal glands

explanation.summary: Topical metronidazole fails in trichomoniasis because T. vaginalis burrows into the urethra and perivaginal glands, where gel cannot reach therapeutic levels; oral therapy is always preferred.
explanation.whyCorrect: T. vaginalis does not just live on the surface of the vaginal canal; it burrows deep into the urethra and perivaginal glands, where topical gels cannot achieve drug levels needed for eradication. That is why the oral route of metronidazole is always preferred for trichomoniasis, unlike BV, where oral or vaginal gel may be used.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Metronidazole is effective against protozoal parasites and is the drug of choice for T. vaginalis; the problem is the route.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Nothing in the lecture attributes topical failure to pH; the explanation is that the gel cannot reach the organism's deeper sites.
whyWrongByChoice.C: T. vaginalis lacks a cyst form; this is why it depends on sexual transmission.
whyWrongByChoice.D: T. vaginalis is a flagellated protozoan, not a yeast.

questions.stem: A 36-year-old woman has vulvar pruritus and a thick white discharge. KOH preparation shows budding yeast with pseudohyphae, and vaginal pH is 4.3. Her friend recently had bacterial vaginosis with a pH of 5.5. Which of the following best explains why this patient's pH remains in the expected range?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Candida secretes lactic acid that re-acidifies the vagina

choices.label: B
choices.text: Candidiasis does not decrease the lactobacillus population

choices.label: C
choices.text: Fungal ergosterol buffers alkaline amines made by anaerobes

choices.label: D
choices.text: Neutrophils in candidiasis consume alkaline bacterial by-products

choices.label: E
choices.text: Yeast suppresses anaerobes by producing volatile amines itself

explanation.summary: Vaginal candidiasis is not associated with loss of lactobacilli, so pH stays 4.0-4.5, unlike BV and trichomoniasis (both above 4.5).
explanation.whyCorrect: Vaginal pH is set by lactobacilli converting sugars to lactic acid. In BV, lactobacilli decline and pH rises above 4.5; in trichomoniasis, inflammation secondarily reduces them. Vaginal candidiasis is not associated with a decrease in lactobacilli, so the pH remains in the expected 4.0-4.5 range, a key discriminating feature.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The acid comes from lactobacilli, not from Candida; the point is that lactobacilli are preserved.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Ergosterol is a fungal membrane sterol (the azole target), not a vaginal pH buffer.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The pH is normal because lactobacilli are intact, not because of any neutrophil effect on bacterial by-products.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Volatile amines come from anaerobic bacterial metabolism in BV; Candida infection has minimal or no odor.

questions.stem: A 27-year-old woman has symptoms suggestive of bacterial vaginosis. The clinician wants the laboratory test regarded as the reference standard, which is more specific for this diagnosis than bedside criteria, and the patient accepts waiting for the result. Which of the following tests should be ordered?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Gram stain of the vaginal discharge sample

choices.label: B
choices.text: KOH preparation to look for pseudohyphae

choices.label: C
choices.text: Saline wet mount scored by Amsel criteria

choices.label: D
choices.text: Vaginal pH measurement with indicator paper

choices.label: E
choices.text: Whiff test with 10% potassium hydroxide

explanation.summary: Gram stain is the reference-standard laboratory test for BV and is more specific than the Amsel criteria, but results are delayed.
explanation.whyCorrect: The Gram stain is the reference standard laboratory test for BV and is more specific than the Amsel criteria. Its drawback is that the sample is sent to a lab, so the diagnosis usually is not available during the office visit.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Pseudohyphae identify Candida and do not diagnose bacterial vaginosis.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The Amsel criteria can be applied in the office, but they rely on clinical diagnosis and leave more room for error than the Gram stain.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Vaginal pH above 4.5 is only one Amsel criterion and is also elevated in trichomoniasis.
whyWrongByChoice.E: A positive whiff test is only one of the four Amsel criteria and is not the reference standard.

questions.stem: A 23-year-old woman with a new sexual partner has a thin, grayish, malodorous vaginal discharge. Unlike typical cases of this discharge pattern, she also reports moderate to severe lower pelvic pain, and examination shows marked vulvovaginal swelling and erythema. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Prescribe single-dose oral fluconazole for presumed yeast

choices.label: B
choices.text: Prescribe topical nystatin and reevaluate her in one month

choices.label: C
choices.text: Reassure her that most such cases resolve without treatment

choices.label: D
choices.text: Test for Neisseria gonorrhoeae and Chlamydia trachomatis

choices.label: E
choices.text: Treat for bacterial vaginosis with metronidazole and no other testing

explanation.summary: Moderate to severe pain or marked inflammation is not typical of BV and should raise suspicion for another infection, including STIs and PID.
explanation.whyCorrect: Pain with BV is usually mild; moderate to severe pain, swelling, or erythema should suggest an infection other than BV, and suspicion for pelvic inflammatory disease should increase. STIs such as N. gonorrhoeae and C. trachomatis cause similar symptoms, can coexist, and if untreated can cause PID, leading to infertility or chronic pain, so they must be ruled out.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Nothing suggests candidiasis (thick white discharge, normal pH); fluconazole would not address a possible STI.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Nystatin is a topical antifungal for mild candidiasis and would delay evaluation of a possible STI.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Self-resolution applies to many mild BV cases, not to a patient with severe pain and inflammation that raise concern for PID.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Treating for BV alone ignores findings that suggest a different or concurrent infection such as an STI with possible PID.

questions.stem: A 52-year-old woman with poorly controlled diabetes mellitus has had three episodes of vulvovaginal candidiasis this year. Which of the following best explains how her hyperglycemia predisposes her to these infections?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It depletes lactobacilli, raising pH so that anaerobes flourish

choices.label: B
choices.text: It impairs leukocyte function, blunting innate defense

choices.label: C
choices.text: It induces Candida to switch into a resistant cyst stage

choices.label: D
choices.text: It kills commensal bacteria, opening a niche for the yeast

choices.label: E
choices.text: It lowers vaginal pH below the range that suppresses yeast

explanation.summary: Hyperglycemia impairs leukocyte function, inhibiting the innate response to Candida.
explanation.whyCorrect: Poorly controlled diabetes, immunosuppression, and antibiotic use increase the likelihood of vaginal candidiasis. Hyperglycemia specifically affects leukocyte function, inhibiting the innate immune response to Candida so colonizing yeast can invade tissue.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Lactobacillus depletion with anaerobic overgrowth is the mechanism of bacterial vaginosis, not candidiasis.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Candida forms yeasts and pseudohyphae, not cysts.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Killing commensal flora to open a niche is how antibiotics predispose to candidiasis, not how hyperglycemia does.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Vaginal candidiasis occurs with a normal pH of 4.0-4.5; the lecture does not describe hyperglycemia acting through pH.

questions.stem: Among patients presenting with vaginitis, which of the following causes accounts for the largest share of cases, roughly 40%-50%?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Bacterial vaginosis

choices.label: B
choices.text: Chlamydial cervicitis

choices.label: C
choices.text: Gonococcal cervicitis

choices.label: D
choices.text: Trichomoniasis

choices.label: E
choices.text: Vulvovaginal candidiasis

explanation.summary: Bacterial vaginosis is the most common cause of vaginitis (about 40%-50% of cases).
explanation.whyCorrect: BV accounts for about 40%-50% of vaginitis cases, followed by Candida (about 20%-25%) and trichomoniasis (about 15%-20%).

whyWrongByChoice.B: Chlamydia likewise must be excluded in the workup but is not the most common cause of vaginitis.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Gonorrhea causes cervicitis with overlapping symptoms and must be ruled out, but it is not the leading cause of vaginitis.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Trichomoniasis is the third most common cause, at about 15%-20% of cases.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Candida is the second most common cause, at about 20%-25% of cases.

questions.stem: During evaluation of a vaginal discharge, a clinician adds a drop of 10% potassium hydroxide to a sample of the fluid, and a strong fishy odor is immediately noted. Which of the following best explains this result?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Alkali activates trichomonad enzymes that produce ammonia

choices.label: B
choices.text: Alkali releases volatile amines made by anaerobic bacteria

choices.label: C
choices.text: KOH denatures cervical mucus into odorous peptides

choices.label: D
choices.text: KOH kills lactobacilli, which then release putrid acids

choices.label: E
choices.text: KOH lyses yeast cell walls, releasing sulfur compounds

explanation.summary: A positive whiff test reflects release of volatile amines, by-products of anaerobic bacterial metabolism, when alkaline KOH is added.
explanation.whyCorrect: In the whiff test, alkaline KOH causes release of volatile amines attributed to anaerobic bacterial metabolic by-products. A positive whiff test is one of the four Amsel criteria for bacterial vaginosis.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The whiff test is an Amsel criterion for BV; the odor is attributed to anaerobic bacterial amines.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The odor is not attributed to mucus; it comes from volatile amines of anaerobic metabolism.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Lactobacilli produce lactic acid and are already reduced in BV; the odor comes from anaerobic amines.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Candida infection has minimal or no odor; the whiff test detects bacterial amines, not yeast products.

questions.stem: A 33-year-old woman with bacterial vaginosis notes that the vaginal odor is much worse in the hours after unprotected intercourse with her male partner. Which of the following best explains this pattern?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Acidic semen converts bacterial by-products into volatile acids

choices.label: B
choices.text: Alkaline semen triggers release of bacterial amine by-products

choices.label: C
choices.text: Friction microtrauma lets trichomonads invade the epithelium

choices.label: D
choices.text: Intercourse boosts lactobacilli, generating excess lactic acid

choices.label: E
choices.text: Semen introduces Candida that ferments glucose into odorants

explanation.summary: BV odor worsens after sex because alkaline semen triggers pH-dependent release of bacterial amines.
explanation.whyCorrect: Odor in BV is noted especially after sexual intercourse because semen is alkaline; exposure to semen triggers pH-dependent release of bacterial by-products such as amines, the same principle as the KOH whiff test.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Semen is alkaline, not acidic, and the odorants are amines.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Microtrauma is proposed to help Candida invade in candidiasis; it does not explain BV odor.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Lactobacilli are reduced in BV, and lactic acid does not produce the fishy odor.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Candida infection has minimal or no odor and is not introduced by semen in this mechanism.

questions.stem: A 25-year-old woman has a thin, gray, homogeneous vaginal discharge. A saline wet mount shows clue cells. Vaginal pH has not yet been measured, and a whiff test has not been performed. Which of the following additional findings would establish the diagnosis of bacterial vaginosis by Amsel criteria?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Budding yeast forms on the KOH preparation

choices.label: B
choices.text: Numerous neutrophils on the saline wet mount

choices.label: C
choices.text: Punctate hemorrhages on the ectocervix

choices.label: D
choices.text: Vaginal pH of 4.2 on indicator paper

choices.label: E
choices.text: Vaginal pH of 5.4 on indicator paper

explanation.summary: Amsel criteria require 3 of 4: gray thin homogeneous discharge, pH above 4.5, positive whiff test, and clue cells.
explanation.whyCorrect: She already meets two Amsel criteria (characteristic discharge and clue cells). A vaginal pH greater than 4.5 would be the third, satisfying the requirement of three of four criteria.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Budding yeast indicate candidiasis and are not an Amsel criterion.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Neutrophils are not an Amsel criterion, and BV characteristically lacks white cells.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Punctate cervical hemorrhages (strawberry cervix) point to trichomoniasis and are not an Amsel criterion.
whyWrongByChoice.D: A pH of 4.2 is in the normal range and does not meet the pH criterion, which requires a value above 4.5.

questions.stem: A 30-year-old woman who lives two hours from the clinic has symptoms suggestive of bacterial vaginosis. She asks whether she can be diagnosed and leave with treatment today. Which of the following approaches is most likely to allow a diagnosis during this visit?

choices.label: A
choices.text: DNA probe sent to a reference laboratory for testing

choices.label: B
choices.text: Empiric topical nystatin with reevaluation next month

choices.label: C
choices.text: Gram stain of discharge sent to the hospital laboratory

choices.label: D
choices.text: Molecular NAAT panel run on a single vaginal swab

choices.label: E
choices.text: Saline wet-mount microscopy applying Amsel criteria

explanation.summary: Amsel criteria on saline wet mount can usually be applied during the office visit.
explanation.whyCorrect: An advantage of the saline wet mount with Amsel criteria is that it can usually be performed during the patient's office visit. The tradeoff is that it depends on clinical judgment and leaves more room for error than laboratory tests.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Sending a sample to an outside laboratory delays the result beyond the visit.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Nystatin is an antifungal for mild candidiasis and does not diagnose or treat BV.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The Gram stain is the reference standard, but the sample is sent to a lab, so a diagnosis usually is not available at the visit.
whyWrongByChoice.D: NAAT results are not available immediately and testing can be expensive.

questions.stem: A clinician evaluating recurrent vaginal discharge wants to test for bacterial vaginosis, Candida, and Trichomonas vaginalis together with the highest sensitivity and specificity from a single swab. Cost and a short delay are acceptable. Which of the following tests is most appropriate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Gram stain of the vaginal discharge

choices.label: B
choices.text: Molecular nucleic acid amplification panel

choices.label: C
choices.text: Saline wet mount scored by Amsel criteria

choices.label: D
choices.text: Vaginal pH testing with indicator paper

choices.label: E
choices.text: Whiff test with potassium hydroxide

explanation.summary: NAAT panels offer greater sensitivity and specificity and can test multiple organisms from one swab, at the cost of expense and delayed results.
explanation.whyCorrect: Molecular (DNA) tests provide greater sensitivity and specificity than the Amsel criteria and Gram stain. Because they are available individually or as a panel, multiple organisms can be tested from a single vaginal swab; results are not immediate and testing can be expensive.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The Gram stain is the reference standard for BV but does not screen for all three causes with NAAT-level accuracy.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The Amsel criteria are a clinical bedside tool for BV only and leave more room for error.
whyWrongByChoice.D: An elevated pH is nonspecific, occurring in both BV and trichomoniasis.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The whiff test is a single Amsel criterion for BV and cannot identify Candida or Trichomonas.

questions.stem: A 20-year-old woman with a new sexual partner has dysuria and a yellow-green malodorous vaginal discharge. Vaginal pH is 5.5. A saline wet mount shows no motile organisms and no clue cells. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Diagnose bacterial vaginosis and prescribe metronidazole gel

choices.label: B
choices.text: Prescribe single-dose oral fluconazole for a likely yeast infection

choices.label: C
choices.text: Reassure her that the negative wet mount excludes Trichomonas

choices.label: D
choices.text: Repeat the wet mount only if her discharge persists for months

choices.label: E
choices.text: Send a nucleic acid amplification test for Trichomonas vaginalis

explanation.summary: NAATs are now first-line for trichomoniasis because they are more sensitive than wet mount.
explanation.whyCorrect: Her yellow-green malodorous discharge, dysuria, high pH, and sexual risk suggest trichomoniasis. The wet mount is the classic test, but NAATs are now first-line because they are more sensitive, so a negative wet mount does not rule out infection.

whyWrongByChoice.A: No clue cells are present, and the yellow-green discharge fits trichomoniasis; topical metronidazole also fails against T. vaginalis.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Candidiasis causes a thick white discharge with a normal pH; this picture does not fit.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The wet mount is less sensitive than NAAT, so a negative result does not exclude trichomoniasis.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Delaying testing leaves a likely STI untreated and transmissible; NAAT is the more sensitive test now.

questions.stem: A Gram stain of vaginal discharge from a woman with bacterial vaginosis shows a mixed population of organisms. In addition to Gardnerella vaginalis, which of the following organisms is commonly associated with this condition?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Candida albicans

choices.label: B
choices.text: Lactobacillus species

choices.label: C
choices.text: Mycoplasma hominis

choices.label: D
choices.text: Treponema pallidum

choices.label: E
choices.text: Trichomonas vaginalis

explanation.summary: Besides G. vaginalis, BV-associated anaerobe groups include Bacteroides, Peptostreptococcus, Fusobacterium, Mycoplasma hominis, and Prevotella.
explanation.whyCorrect: BV is an overgrowth of anaerobic and BV-associated organisms. In addition to G. vaginalis, common groups include Bacteroides, Peptostreptococcus, Fusobacterium, Mycoplasma hominis, and Prevotella.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Candida causes vulvovaginal candidiasis, a separate condition with a normal pH.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Lactobacilli decrease in BV; their loss is what permits anaerobic overgrowth.
whyWrongByChoice.D: T. pallidum causes syphilis, an STI to rule out, not a BV-associated organism.
whyWrongByChoice.E: T. vaginalis is a protozoan causing trichomoniasis, a separate infection.

questions.stem: A 32-year-old woman is diagnosed with bacterial vaginosis. Which of the following elements of her history is most likely to have contributed to this condition?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Abstinence from sexual activity for the past year

choices.label: B
choices.text: Consistent barrier protection during intercourse

choices.label: C
choices.text: Discontinuing all intravaginal hygiene products

choices.label: D
choices.text: No antibiotic use during the past two years

choices.label: E
choices.text: Recent placement of an intrauterine device

explanation.summary: IUD use is among the microbiome-disrupting risk factors for BV.
explanation.whyCorrect: Activities that disrupt the vaginal microbiome increase BV risk: douching, recent antibiotic use, intravaginal hygiene products, IUD use, multiple or new sexual partners, and concurrent STIs.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Abstinent people can develop BV, but abstinence is not a risk factor.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Barrier protection may reduce BV occurrence rather than cause it.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Intravaginal hygiene products are a risk factor, so stopping them lowers risk.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Recent antibiotic use is a risk factor; its absence does not contribute.

questions.stem: The organism most important in causing bacterial vaginosis is identified on a Gram stain of vaginal discharge. Which of the following best describes how this organism is classified?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Flagellated pear-shaped protozoan

choices.label: B
choices.text: Gram-negative diplococcus

choices.label: C
choices.text: Gram-positive rod that produces lactic acid

choices.label: D
choices.text: Gram-variable coccobacillus

choices.label: E
choices.text: Yeast that forms pseudohyphae and germ tubes

explanation.summary: Gardnerella vaginalis is a gram-variable coccobacillus.
explanation.whyCorrect: Gardnerella vaginalis, the most important causative organism of BV, is a bacterium classified as a gram-variable coccobacillus. It flourishes with loss of vaginal Lactobacillus and a pH above 4.5.

whyWrongByChoice.A: This describes Trichomonas vaginalis.
whyWrongByChoice.B: A gram-negative diplococcus describes N. gonorrhoeae, a cause of cervicitis.
whyWrongByChoice.C: This describes the protective lactobacilli, which decline in BV.
whyWrongByChoice.E: This describes Candida, the cause of vulvovaginal candidiasis.

questions.stem: A vaginal isolate from a symptomatic patient is incubated in serum in the laboratory, where it produces germ tubes. Which of the following best describes this organism?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Anaerobic bacterium that produces volatile amines

choices.label: B
choices.text: Gram-variable coccobacillus that raises vaginal pH

choices.label: C
choices.text: Obligate fungal pathogen that never colonizes healthy hosts

choices.label: D
choices.text: Opportunistic yeast that commonly colonizes the vagina

choices.label: E
choices.text: Protozoan that survives only in the genitourinary tract

explanation.summary: Candida is a yeast, part of the normal flora and an opportunistic pathogen, that forms pseudohyphae in most samples but germ tubes in serum.
explanation.whyCorrect: Germ-tube formation in serum identifies Candida, a fungus (yeast). Candida spp. are normal flora (present in about 25% of vaginas) and act as opportunistic pathogens, causing vaginitis when they invade tissue.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Volatile amines come from BV-associated anaerobes, not from a germ-tube-forming organism.
whyWrongByChoice.B: This describes Gardnerella vaginalis of bacterial vaginosis.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Candida is normal flora in many people and causes disease opportunistically.
whyWrongByChoice.E: This describes T. vaginalis, which does not form germ tubes.

questions.stem: A 29-year-old woman with no vaginal symptoms has a normal pelvic examination. Incidental microscopy of vaginal secretions shows a few yeast cells without evidence of inflammation. Which of the following is the best interpretation?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Bacterial vaginosis that requires oral metronidazole

choices.label: B
choices.text: Commensal colonization; disease requires tissue invasion

choices.label: C
choices.text: Early trichomoniasis that will progress without therapy

choices.label: D
choices.text: Invasive candidiasis that requires an oral azole regimen

choices.label: E
choices.text: Sexually transmitted infection requiring partner therapy

explanation.summary: Candida is part of normal vaginal flora in about 25% of people; vaginitis occurs only when it invades tissue.
explanation.whyCorrect: Candida spp. are often part of the normal vaginal flora (about 25%) and are usually just colonizers. Vaginitis occurs when Candida invades the tissue, producing pruritus, erythema, edema, and discharge, none of which are present here.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Yeast cells do not indicate BV, which shows clue cells and a pH above 4.5.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Yeast cells are not trichomonads, which appear as flagellated pyriform protozoa.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Oral regimens are reserved for severe, recurrent, or immunocompromised presentations, and she has no disease at all.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Vaginal candidiasis is not considered an STI, and partners are treated only if symptomatic.

questions.stem: A 24-year-old woman completes a 10-day course of oral antibiotics for a respiratory infection. Several days later she develops vulvar itching and a thick, white, clumped discharge. Which of the following best explains the link between the antibiotics and her new condition?

choices.label: A
choices.text: They damaged the epithelium, letting trichomonads invade

choices.label: B
choices.text: They increased lactobacilli, over-acidifying the vagina

choices.label: C
choices.text: They induced Candida to switch into a cyst stage

choices.label: D
choices.text: They raised blood glucose and impaired her leukocytes

choices.label: E
choices.text: They suppressed normal flora, opening a niche for yeast

explanation.summary: Antibiotics inhibit normal flora, opening the niche for opportunistic Candida infection.
explanation.whyCorrect: Antibiotic use is a specific risk factor for vaginal candidiasis because antibiotics inhibit the growth of normal flora, opening the niche for opportunistic infections such as Candida.

whyWrongByChoice.A: T. vaginalis is acquired sexually; antibiotics do not cause it, and the discharge described is typical of candidiasis.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Antibiotics inhibit, rather than increase, normal bacterial flora.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Candida forms yeasts and pseudohyphae, not cysts.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Impaired leukocyte function is how hyperglycemia predisposes to candidiasis, not antibiotics.

questions.stem: A 27-year-old woman is treated for vulvovaginal candidiasis. She asks whether her husband, who has no genital complaints, also needs treatment. Which of the following is the most appropriate response?

choices.label: A
choices.text: No, because Candida never colonizes any human mucosa

choices.label: B
choices.text: No, partners are treated only if they have symptoms

choices.label: C
choices.text: Yes, because candidiasis is a sexually transmitted infection

choices.label: D
choices.text: Yes, with dual oral and topical antifungal therapy

choices.label: E
choices.text: Yes, with oral metronidazole to prevent her recurrence

explanation.summary: In vaginal candidiasis, sexual partners are not treated unless they have symptoms.
explanation.whyCorrect: Vaginal candidiasis is not considered an STI, although sexual activity increases risk, possibly via epithelial microtrauma. It is not important for sexual partners to be treated unless they have symptoms.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Candida normally lives in the vagina, mouth, throat, and gut.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Vaginal candidiasis is not considered an STI.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Dual oral and topical partner therapy is the lecture's recommendation for male partners in BV, not candidiasis.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Metronidazole treats BV and trichomoniasis, not yeast, and partner treatment is not needed here.

questions.stem: A 35-year-old woman has vaginal burning and itching. Speculum examination reveals erythema and edema of the vulva and vaginal mucosa with a thick, white discharge adherent to the vaginal walls. Which of the following additional findings is most consistent with the likely diagnosis?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Frothy yellow-green malodorous discharge

choices.label: B
choices.text: Motile flagellated organisms on wet mount

choices.label: C
choices.text: Normal-appearing cervix and minimal odor

choices.label: D
choices.text: Punctate hemorrhages dotting the cervix

choices.label: E
choices.text: Vaginal pH of 5.8 with a positive whiff test

explanation.summary: In vaginal candidiasis, the cervix appears normal (as in BV, unlike trichomoniasis) and there is minimal or no odor.
explanation.whyCorrect: Vulvovaginal erythema and edema with a cottage cheese-like discharge indicate vaginal candidiasis. In this condition there is minimal or no odor, and the cervix appears normal, as in BV but in contrast to the strawberry cervix of trichomoniasis.

whyWrongByChoice.A: A frothy yellow-green malodorous discharge is characteristic of trichomoniasis.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Motile flagellated protozoa indicate T. vaginalis.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Punctate cervical hemorrhages (strawberry cervix) indicate trichomoniasis.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Candidiasis keeps a pH of 4.0-4.5, and a positive whiff test points to BV.

questions.stem: A 30-year-old woman without symptoms has a routine screening test that is positive for Trichomonas vaginalis. She is surprised because she feels well. Which of the following statements about this infection is most accurate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Asymptomatic carriage is typical of candidiasis, not this one

choices.label: B
choices.text: Asymptomatic results are false positives needing repeat tests

choices.label: C
choices.text: Most infected people, including most men, have no symptoms

choices.label: D
choices.text: The organism stays in the vagina and cannot reach the cervix

choices.label: E
choices.text: Without symptoms she needs no treatment for the infection

explanation.summary: About 70% of people with trichomoniasis are asymptomatic, and male infection is typically asymptomatic.
explanation.whyCorrect: The majority of individuals with trichomoniasis (about 70%) are asymptomatic, and infection of the male genitourinary tract is typically asymptomatic as well. Trichomoniasis is a true STI and is treated with oral metronidazole for her and her partner.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Most people with trichomoniasis are asymptomatic.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Asymptomatic infection is the norm, so a positive result in a well patient is expected rather than suspect.
whyWrongByChoice.D: T. vaginalis can also infect the cervix, endometrium, and Bartholin glands.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Trichomoniasis should be treated with antibiotics even when asymptomatic, given its sexual transmission.

questions.stem: Unlike many other protozoa that infect humans, Trichomonas vaginalis is transmitted almost exclusively through sexual intercourse. Which of the following features of the organism best explains this?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Animal reservoirs maintain it between human infections

choices.label: B
choices.text: It forms hardy cysts that are shed in stool and ingested

choices.label: C
choices.text: It is normal gut flora that seeds the vagina from the rectum

choices.label: D
choices.text: It lacks a cyst stage and survives only in the genital tract

choices.label: E
choices.text: It spreads on shared fomites as environmentally resistant spores

explanation.summary: T. vaginalis lacks a cyst form and survives only in the human genitourinary tract, so it is transmitted sexually.
explanation.whyCorrect: T. vaginalis can survive for significant periods only within the human genitourinary tract, and humans are its only known natural host. It lacks the cyst form common to many other protozoa, so transmission occurs primarily through sexual intercourse.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Humans are the only known natural host.
whyWrongByChoice.B: T. vaginalis lacks a cyst form and predominantly involves the urogenital tract, not the GI tract.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Infection predominantly involves the urogenital tract rather than gastrointestinal sites; it is not normal gut flora.
whyWrongByChoice.E: It does not form spores; it survives only in the human genitourinary tract.

questions.stem: A 34-year-old man is informed that his female partner has trichomoniasis. He has no symptoms and asks where in his body the organism could be living. Which of the following sites are most commonly colonized in men?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Bloodstream and lymph nodes

choices.label: B
choices.text: Colon and rectal mucosa

choices.label: C
choices.text: Oropharynx and tonsillar crypts

choices.label: D
choices.text: Penile urethra and prostate

choices.label: E
choices.text: Scrotal skin and inguinal folds

explanation.summary: T. vaginalis commonly colonizes the vaginal epithelium, penile urethra, and prostate.
explanation.whyCorrect: T. vaginalis commonly colonizes the vaginal epithelium, penile urethra, and prostate. Male infection is typically asymptomatic, which is why the partner is treated even without symptoms.

whyWrongByChoice.A: T. vaginalis is not described as a bloodstream or lymphatic infection; it lives in the genitourinary tract.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Infection predominantly involves the urogenital tract rather than gastrointestinal sites.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Infection predominantly involves the urogenital tract rather than oral sites.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The organism colonizes the urethra and prostate, not the external skin.

questions.stem: A 25-year-old woman with trichomoniasis has an erythematous, tender vaginal mucosa, and a wet mount of her discharge shows abundant white blood cells along with the organisms. Which of the following best describes the mechanism producing her inflammation?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Anaerobic overgrowth that provokes no inflammatory response

choices.label: B
choices.text: Chronic lymphocytic infiltrate from persistent antigen

choices.label: C
choices.text: Cytotoxic epithelial damage drawing a neutrophilic response

choices.label: D
choices.text: Immune complex deposition within the vaginal wall

choices.label: E
choices.text: Yeast invasion permitted by impaired leukocyte function

explanation.summary: T. vaginalis releases cytotoxic substances that damage the epithelium, triggering neutrophil-predominant inflammation.
explanation.whyCorrect: Infection of the vaginal epithelium causes direct epithelial damage through released cytotoxic substances. The damage triggers a neutrophil-predominant inflammatory response, producing discharge, irritation, and discomfort; the inflammation also secondarily reduces lactobacilli and raises pH above 4.5.

whyWrongByChoice.A: This describes BV, which has little inflammation and no white cells.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The response is neutrophil-predominant, not lymphocytic.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Immune complex deposition is not the lecture's mechanism for trichomoniasis.
whyWrongByChoice.E: This describes candidiasis in hyperglycemia.

questions.stem: On speculum examination of a 21-year-old woman with vaginal itching, the cervix is covered with innumerable tiny red dots, giving it a strawberry-like appearance. Which of the following best describes these lesions?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Adherent curd-like fungal exudate on the cervix

choices.label: B
choices.text: Epithelial cells coated with adherent bacteria

choices.label: C
choices.text: Healed scars from prior cervical instrumentation

choices.label: D
choices.text: Hyperkeratotic white plaques over the ectocervix

choices.label: E
choices.text: Punctate capillary hemorrhages on the cervix

explanation.summary: Strawberry cervix (colpitis macularis) consists of punctate capillary hemorrhages and is pathognomonic for trichomoniasis involving the outer cervix.
explanation.whyCorrect: When T. vaginalis involves the outer cervix, it causes irritation with tiny capillary hemorrhages that look like red dots, producing the pathognomonic 'strawberry cervix' (colpitis macularis).

whyWrongByChoice.A: Curd-like exudate describes the cottage cheese discharge of candidiasis, in which the cervix appears normal.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Bacteria-coated epithelial cells are clue cells seen microscopically in BV, which has a noninflamed cervix.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The lesions are active punctate hemorrhages from T. vaginalis infection, not scars.
whyWrongByChoice.D: White plaques are not the strawberry cervix lesion, which consists of red punctate hemorrhages.

questions.stem: A 38-year-old woman is prescribed oral metronidazole for bacterial vaginosis. She asks how the medication works. Which of the following best describes its mechanism of action?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Binds the 50S ribosome to halt protein synthesis

choices.label: B
choices.text: Blocks peptidoglycan cross-linking in the cell wall

choices.label: C
choices.text: Enters the cell and forms free radicals that damage DNA

choices.label: D
choices.text: Inhibits ergosterol synthesis in the cell membrane

choices.label: E
choices.text: Restores lactobacilli by acidifying vaginal fluid

explanation.summary: Metronidazole enters the cell, forms free radicals, destroys intracellular components including DNA, and causes cell death.
explanation.whyCorrect: Metronidazole enters the bacterial cell and forms free radicals that destroy intracellular components, including DNA, causing cell death. It is effective against many gram-positive and gram-negative anaerobes and protozoal parasites, which is why it treats both BV and trichomoniasis.

whyWrongByChoice.A: This is not metronidazole's mechanism; it acts through DNA-damaging free radicals.
whyWrongByChoice.B: This is not metronidazole's mechanism; it acts through DNA-damaging free radicals.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Ergosterol synthesis inhibition is the mechanism of azole antifungals used for candidiasis.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Metronidazole kills organisms directly; it does not act by acidifying vaginal fluid.

questions.stem: A 40-year-old woman has her third episode of bacterial vaginosis in a year. She douches several times a week and uses scented intravaginal washes. In addition to metronidazole, which of the following recommendations is most likely to reduce her recurrences?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Add a daily scented intravaginal cleanser

choices.label: B
choices.text: Apply topical nystatin after every menstrual period

choices.label: C
choices.text: Avoid condoms to preserve the normal vaginal flora

choices.label: D
choices.text: Douche immediately after each episode of intercourse

choices.label: E
choices.text: Stop douching and intravaginal hygiene products

explanation.summary: Excessive vaginal cleaning such as douching increases BV; changing hygiene habits is often effective.
explanation.whyCorrect: Douching and intravaginal hygiene products disrupt the vaginal microbiome and increase BV risk. Changing hygiene habits is often effective, and barrier protection may also reduce occurrence.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Intravaginal hygiene products are a BV risk factor.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Nystatin is an antifungal for candidiasis and does not prevent BV.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Barrier protection may reduce BV; avoiding condoms would not help.
whyWrongByChoice.D: More douching further disrupts the vaginal microbiome and increases BV risk.

questions.stem: A 29-year-old woman has confirmed bacterial vaginosis for the third time this year despite completing metronidazole each time and stopping douching. She has one male partner. According to the approach taught for this condition, which of the following is recommended for her partner?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Dual oral and topical antibiotic therapy to reduce her recurrence

choices.label: B
choices.text: No therapy, because sexual activity plays no role in this condition

choices.label: C
choices.text: Single-dose oral fluconazole to eliminate yeast colonization

choices.label: D
choices.text: Therapy only if he later develops a urethral discharge

choices.label: E
choices.text: Topical clotrimazole cream applied daily for one week

explanation.summary: The lecture recommends dual oral and topical antibiotic treatment of male partners of patients with confirmed BV to reduce recurrence.
explanation.whyCorrect: Although BV is not an STI, sexual practices contribute to risk. The lecture recommends that male sexual partners of female patients with confirmed BV be treated with dual oral and topical antibiotic therapy to reduce the risk of recurrence in the female patient.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Sexual practices do contribute to BV risk even though BV is not an STI.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Fluconazole is an antifungal for candidiasis and does not address BV organisms.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The recommendation is to treat male partners of confirmed BV patients, not to wait for symptoms.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Clotrimazole is a topical antifungal and is not the recommended partner therapy for BV.

questions.stem: A 45-year-old woman receiving chemotherapy for lymphoma has recurrent, extensive vulvovaginal candidiasis with deep tissue involvement. Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment approach?

choices.label: A
choices.text: An oral azole antifungal regimen

choices.label: B
choices.text: Oral metronidazole for her and her partner

choices.label: C
choices.text: Topical clotrimazole cream for one week

choices.label: D
choices.text: Topical nystatin applied to the vulva

choices.label: E
choices.text: Watchful waiting until it resolves on its own

explanation.summary: Oral antifungal regimens are used for severe candidiasis: deep tissue involvement, recurrent infection, or an immunocompromised patient.
explanation.whyCorrect: Topical antifungals (nystatin, clotrimazole) are for milder, localized symptoms. Oral antifungal regimens are prescribed for more severe presentations such as deep tissue involvement, recurrent infections, or immunocompromised patients; azoles act by inhibiting ergosterol synthesis.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Metronidazole treats BV and trichomoniasis, not fungal infection.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Topical clotrimazole is likewise reserved for milder, localized disease.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Topical nystatin is for milder, localized symptoms, not recurrent deep disease in an immunocompromised patient.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Candidiasis can self-resolve in mild cases, but this severe presentation in an immunocompromised patient needs treatment.

questions.stem: A 23-year-old man has had 2 days of painful urination and a copious, frankly purulent penile discharge that began abruptly. There are no lesions on the external genitalia. Which of the following organisms is the most likely cause?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Chlamydia trachomatis

choices.label: B
choices.text: Escherichia coli

choices.label: C
choices.text: Herpes simplex virus

choices.label: D
choices.text: Neisseria gonorrhoeae

choices.label: E
choices.text: Staphylococcus saprophyticus

explanation.summary: An acute, frankly purulent urethral discharge suggests gonorrhea rather than chlamydia.
explanation.whyCorrect: N. gonorrhoeae and C. trachomatis are the two most important causes of urethritis and are often clinically indistinguishable. Gonorrhea, however, tends to be more acute, and a frankly purulent penile discharge points toward N. gonorrhoeae.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Chlamydia is more often subacute or unnoticed; dysuria alone with little discharge is more typical of C. trachomatis.
whyWrongByChoice.B: E. coli is a leading cause of cystitis, which typically does not produce urethral discharge.
whyWrongByChoice.C: HSV is suggested by external genital ulcers, fever, and tender inguinal lymphadenopathy, none of which are present.
whyWrongByChoice.E: S. saprophyticus causes urinary tract infections, not purulent STI urethritis.

questions.topicName: Urethritis, Cervicitis, and Pelvic Inflammatory Disease

questions.stem: A 20-year-old woman has mucopurulent cervical discharge and mild dysuria. Her clinician wants the single most accurate test to identify the causative pathogen. Which of the following is the gold standard?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Bacterial culture of a cervical swab

choices.label: B
choices.text: Diagnostic laparoscopy

choices.label: C
choices.text: Gram stain of cervical exudate

choices.label: D
choices.text: Nucleic acid amplification testing

choices.label: E
choices.text: Transvaginal ultrasonography

explanation.summary: NAAT is the gold standard diagnostic test for urethritis and cervicitis.
explanation.whyCorrect: NAAT is rapid and highly sensitive and can detect C. trachomatis, N. gonorrhoeae, M. genitalium, HSV, and other agents from a swab or urine specimen. It is the gold standard for diagnosing urethritis and cervicitis.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Culture is time consuming; its main value is determining antibiotic susceptibility.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Laparoscopy is the best test for uncertain PID, not for diagnosing cervicitis.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Gram stain is seldom used because C. trachomatis and viruses cannot be seen and the sample may be insufficient.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Transvaginal ultrasonography images pelvic structures and cannot identify an organism in cervicitis.

questions.topicName: Urethritis, Cervicitis, and Pelvic Inflammatory Disease

questions.stem: A 26-year-old man has dysuria, fever, and headache. Examination shows several painful shallow ulcers on the penile shaft and tender bilateral inguinal lymphadenopathy. Which of the following is the most likely cause?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Chlamydia trachomatis

choices.label: B
choices.text: Herpes simplex virus

choices.label: C
choices.text: Mycoplasma genitalium

choices.label: D
choices.text: Neisseria gonorrhoeae

choices.label: E
choices.text: Trichomonas vaginalis

explanation.summary: Genital ulcers with fever, headache, and tender inguinal nodes point to HSV rather than gonorrhea or chlamydia.
explanation.whyCorrect: When urethritis is accompanied by genital ulceration or other external lesions, a cause other than N. gonorrhoeae or C. trachomatis should be sought. External genital ulcers are strongly associated with HSV, which also causes fever, tender local inguinal lymphadenopathy, and headache.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Chlamydia causes subacute urethritis and does not produce the ulcers seen here.
whyWrongByChoice.C: M. genitalium is an increasingly recognized cause of urethritis but not of ulcerative lesions.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Gonorrhea causes urethritis with purulent discharge but does not explain genital ulcers.
whyWrongByChoice.E: T. vaginalis can cause urethritis but is not associated with genital ulcers and tender adenopathy.

questions.topicName: Urethritis, Cervicitis, and Pelvic Inflammatory Disease

questions.stem: A 25-year-old woman has had worsening lower abdominal pain for 2 days and a temperature of 38.4°C. During bimanual examination, she cries out and lifts her hips off the table when the clinician gently moves the cervix. Which of the following conditions does this finding most strongly suggest?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Acute bacterial cystitis

choices.label: B
choices.text: Acute pyelonephritis

choices.label: C
choices.text: Isolated gonococcal urethritis

choices.label: D
choices.text: Pelvic inflammatory disease

choices.label: E
choices.text: Vaginal cellulitis

explanation.summary: Cervical motion tenderness (the chandelier sign) indicates PID.
explanation.whyCorrect: Bimanual findings that indicate PID are lower abdominal tenderness, adnexal tenderness, and cervical motion tenderness. The last is called the chandelier sign because manipulation of the cervix is so painful the patient seems to leap toward the chandelier.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Cystitis is a lower urinary tract infection and does not produce cervical motion tenderness.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Pyelonephritis is an upper urinary tract infection of the kidney and does not cause cervical motion tenderness.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Isolated urethritis presents with dysuria and discharge, not fever and severe pain on cervical movement.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Vaginal cellulitis is a localized soft tissue infection of the vaginal wall, not an upper tract inflammation.

questions.topicName: Urethritis, Cervicitis, and Pelvic Inflammatory Disease

questions.stem: Ascending gonococcal and chlamydial infections in females can progress to peritonitis and sepsis, whereas upper reproductive tract infections in males generally cause less severe systemic illness. Which of the following anatomic features best explains this difference?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The cervix normally provides no barrier to vaginal organisms

choices.label: B
choices.text: The endometrium is normally colonized by vaginal organisms

choices.label: C
choices.text: The fallopian tubes open directly into the peritoneal cavity

choices.label: D
choices.text: The ovaries form a closed system with the fallopian tubes

choices.label: E
choices.text: The shorter female urethra lets organisms reach the bladder

explanation.summary: The open fimbriated ends of the fallopian tubes let pathogens spill into the peritoneum.
explanation.whyCorrect: The fallopian tubes open into the peritoneal cavity and do not form a closed system with the ovaries. Bacteria can therefore spill into the peritoneum and reach the blood, causing peritonitis and sepsis. The male tract has no such opening, so men generally do not become as sick.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The cervix normally functions as a barrier protecting the sterile upper tract.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The upper reproductive tract, including the uterus, is normally sterile.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The tubes and ovaries do not form a closed system; that openness is the problem.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Urethral length relates to bladder infection, not to spread of infection into the peritoneum.

questions.topicName: Urethritis, Cervicitis, and Pelvic Inflammatory Disease

questions.stem: A 24-year-old woman is diagnosed with pelvic inflammatory disease. Her cervical NAAT is pending. The clinician prescribes ceftriaxone and doxycycline and also adds metronidazole. Which of the following is the primary reason for adding metronidazole?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Coverage of anaerobic vaginal flora

choices.label: B
choices.text: Coverage of Candida species

choices.label: C
choices.text: Coverage of herpes simplex virus

choices.label: D
choices.text: Coverage of Mycoplasma genitalium

choices.label: E
choices.text: Coverage of Staphylococcus saprophyticus

explanation.summary: PID is polymicrobial, so therapy must cover gonorrhea, chlamydia, and anaerobic vaginal flora.
explanation.whyCorrect: Although PID usually begins with N. gonorrhoeae or C. trachomatis, a compromised cervix lets opportunistic vaginal and gastrointestinal organisms (e.g., Prevotella, Leptotrichia, Atopobium) ascend. Treatment must therefore also cover anaerobic vaginal flora, which is the role of metronidazole.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Candida is a fungus and is not the reason metronidazole is included.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Metronidazole has no antiviral activity; HSV is not the target of the PID regimen.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Metronidazole is not added to target M. genitalium in the PID regimen.
whyWrongByChoice.E: S. saprophyticus is a urinary tract pathogen, not part of the PID coverage rationale.

questions.topicName: Urethritis, Cervicitis, and Pelvic Inflammatory Disease

questions.stem: A 29-year-old woman has an atypical 5-day history of vague pelvic pain and low-grade fever. Bimanual examination findings are equivocal, transvaginal ultrasonography is nondiagnostic, and several other causes of abdominopelvic pain remain under consideration. Which of the following is the best test to establish whether she has pelvic inflammatory disease?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Blood cultures from two sites

choices.label: B
choices.text: Complete blood count with differential

choices.label: C
choices.text: Diagnostic laparoscopy

choices.label: D
choices.text: Gram stain of cervical exudate

choices.label: E
choices.text: Repeat transvaginal ultrasonography

explanation.summary: Diagnostic laparoscopy is the best test for PID, reserved for uncertain or atypical cases.
explanation.whyCorrect: PID is usually a clinical diagnosis. Diagnostic laparoscopy is the best test because it directly identifies inflammation and infection, but because it is invasive it is reserved for uncertain diagnoses or atypical presentations such as this one.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Blood cultures are often negative in PID and cannot establish the diagnosis.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Leukocytosis is common but nonspecific and cannot confirm PID.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Gram stain cannot visualize C. trachomatis and does not confirm upper tract inflammation.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Transvaginal ultrasonography has poor sensitivity and specificity for PID; repeating it adds little.

questions.topicName: Urethritis, Cervicitis, and Pelvic Inflammatory Disease

questions.stem: A 27-year-old woman recently treated for pelvic inflammatory disease develops right upper quadrant pain that worsens with deep breathing and coughing. Liver enzymes are normal. Laparoscopy shows thin fibrous bands stretching from the surface of the liver to the anterior abdominal wall. Which of the following structures is primarily inflamed?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Common bile duct epithelium

choices.label: B
choices.text: Gallbladder mucosa

choices.label: C
choices.text: Glisson capsule

choices.label: D
choices.text: Hepatocellular parenchyma

choices.label: E
choices.text: Right diaphragmatic muscle

explanation.summary: Fitz-Hugh-Curtis syndrome is perihepatitis of the Glisson capsule, not the liver parenchyma.
explanation.whyCorrect: About 10% of PID cases result in perihepatitis (Fitz-Hugh-Curtis syndrome), an inflammation of the Glisson capsule surrounding the liver. It causes RUQ pain worsened by breathing, coughing, or movement and produces thin violin-string adhesions between the liver capsule and the anterior abdominal wall or diaphragm.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The biliary tree is not the site of inflammation in this PID complication.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Gallbladder inflammation does not produce violin-string adhesions from the liver surface after PID.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Fitz-Hugh-Curtis spares the parenchyma; it is a capsular inflammation.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Adhesions may reach the diaphragm, but the inflamed structure is the liver capsule.

questions.topicName: Urethritis, Cervicitis, and Pelvic Inflammatory Disease

questions.stem: A 22-year-old woman with cervicitis has a cervical culture that grows Neisseria gonorrhoeae. No testing for Chlamydia trachomatis was sent, and she is not pregnant. Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Azithromycin 1000 mg orally as one dose alone

choices.label: B
choices.text: Ceftriaxone IM once plus doxycycline for 7 days

choices.label: C
choices.text: Ceftriaxone IM once plus metronidazole for 14 days

choices.label: D
choices.text: Ceftriaxone IM once with no additional agent

choices.label: E
choices.text: Doxycycline for 7 days with no ceftriaxone

explanation.summary: Gonococcal cervicitis is treated with single-dose IM ceftriaxone, adding 7 days of doxycycline when chlamydia has not been excluded.
explanation.whyCorrect: The recommended treatment for gonococcal urethritis or cervicitis is a single intramuscular dose of ceftriaxone. Because chlamydial infection has not been excluded in this patient, doxycycline for 7 days is added.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Single-dose azithromycin is the adherence alternative for nongonococcal infection, not gonorrhea therapy.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Metronidazole for 14 days is part of the PID regimen, not the treatment of uncomplicated cervicitis.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Ceftriaxone alone is appropriate only once chlamydia has been excluded.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Doxycycline alone is for nongonococcal infection and does not treat her confirmed gonorrhea.

questions.topicName: Urethritis, Cervicitis, and Pelvic Inflammatory Disease

questions.stem: A 26-year-old woman at 14 weeks' gestation has mucopurulent cervical discharge. NAAT is positive for both Neisseria gonorrhoeae and Chlamydia trachomatis. Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Azithromycin as a single dose alone

choices.label: B
choices.text: Ceftriaxone IM plus azithromycin as a single dose

choices.label: C
choices.text: Ceftriaxone IM plus doxycycline for 7 days

choices.label: D
choices.text: Ceftriaxone IM plus metronidazole for 14 days

choices.label: E
choices.text: Doxycycline for 7 days as sole therapy

explanation.summary: In pregnancy, gonorrhea is still treated with ceftriaxone, but chlamydia is treated with single-dose azithromycin instead of doxycycline.
explanation.whyCorrect: Ceftriaxone remains the recommended treatment for gonorrhea during pregnancy. When chlamydial treatment is also needed in pregnancy, azithromycin as a single dose is used rather than doxycycline.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Azithromycin alone treats the chlamydia but leaves the gonorrhea without ceftriaxone.
whyWrongByChoice.C: This is the nonpregnant regimen; doxycycline is avoided for chlamydia in pregnancy.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Metronidazole covers anaerobes in PID and does not treat chlamydia.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Doxycycline is avoided in pregnancy and does not treat her gonorrhea.

questions.topicName: Urethritis, Cervicitis, and Pelvic Inflammatory Disease

questions.stem: A 21-year-old nonpregnant woman is diagnosed with mild-to-moderate pelvic inflammatory disease. She is tolerating oral intake, appears well, and has no adnexal mass on ultrasonography. Which of the following is the most appropriate outpatient regimen?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Azithromycin 1000 mg once plus metronidazole for 7 days

choices.label: B
choices.text: Ceftriaxone IM once plus azithromycin 1000 mg once

choices.label: C
choices.text: Ceftriaxone IM once plus doxycycline alone for 7 days

choices.label: D
choices.text: Ceftriaxone IM once plus doxycycline and metronidazole for 14 days

choices.label: E
choices.text: Doxycycline and metronidazole for 7 days without ceftriaxone

explanation.summary: Outpatient PID therapy is ceftriaxone IM once plus 14 days of doxycycline and metronidazole.
explanation.whyCorrect: PID is polymicrobial, so therapy must cover N. gonorrhoeae, C. trachomatis, and anaerobic vaginal flora. Mild-to-moderate PID can usually be treated as an outpatient with ceftriaxone IM once plus doxycycline and metronidazole, both for 14 days.

whyWrongByChoice.A: This omits gonococcal coverage and is too short.
whyWrongByChoice.B: This lacks anaerobic coverage and the 14-day course required for PID.
whyWrongByChoice.C: This is the gonococcal cervicitis regimen; it lacks anaerobic coverage and is too short for PID.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Omitting ceftriaxone leaves gonorrhea uncovered, and 7 days is too short for PID.

questions.topicName: Urethritis, Cervicitis, and Pelvic Inflammatory Disease

questions.stem: A 24-year-old nonpregnant woman began outpatient therapy for pelvic inflammatory disease 3 days ago. She has taken every dose, yet her fever and pelvic pain are unchanged. Transvaginal ultrasonography shows no adnexal fluid collection. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Admit to the hospital for parenteral antibiotic therapy

choices.label: B
choices.text: Continue the same oral regimen for the full 14 days

choices.label: C
choices.text: Schedule elective adnexectomy on an outpatient basis

choices.label: D
choices.text: Stop antibiotics and repeat cervical NAAT in 1 week

choices.label: E
choices.text: Switch to single-dose oral azithromycin monotherapy

explanation.summary: Failure to improve within 72 hours of outpatient PID therapy is an indication for hospitalization and parenteral therapy.
explanation.whyCorrect: Hospitalization and parenteral therapy are appropriate for patients who are pregnant, have a tubo-ovarian abscess or severe illness, cannot tolerate outpatient therapy, fail to improve within 72 hours, or need evaluation for a surgical emergency. After clinical improvement, oral doxycycline and metronidazole complete 14 days.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Continuing an unsuccessful outpatient regimen ignores failure to improve within 72 hours.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Adnexectomy is reserved for severe tubo-ovarian abscess, which she does not have.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Stopping treatment risks long-term complications such as infertility and abscess.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Azithromycin monotherapy lacks gonococcal and anaerobic coverage for PID.

questions.topicName: Urethritis, Cervicitis, and Pelvic Inflammatory Disease

questions.stem: A 30-year-old man reports burning with urination and intermittent penile discharge. Before his examination, the clinician asks him not to void. Which of the following best explains this instruction?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A full bladder improves visualization of the meatus

choices.label: B
choices.text: Bladder distension makes urethral stripping less painful

choices.label: C
choices.text: Recent urination causes spasm that hides the meatus

choices.label: D
choices.text: Urination temporarily flushes out exudate and organisms

choices.label: E
choices.text: Urine acidity inactivates the reagents used for NAAT

explanation.summary: Examine for urethritis before the patient urinates so discharge and organisms are not washed away.
explanation.whyCorrect: Urination may temporarily wash away urethral discharge and culturable pathogens. If possible, the urethra should be examined when the patient has not recently urinated.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Bladder volume does not affect visualization of the urethral meatus.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Bladder distension is not the reason for the instruction.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Urination does not cause spasm that conceals the meatus.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Urine is an acceptable NAAT specimen; it does not inactivate the test.

questions.topicName: Urethritis, Cervicitis, and Pelvic Inflammatory Disease

questions.stem: A 24-year-old woman has dysuria, but no discharge is visible at the urethral meatus on initial inspection. Which of the following maneuvers is most appropriate to evaluate for urethral discharge?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Collecting the first stream of a voided urine sample

choices.label: B
choices.text: Inserting a swab into the cervical os and rotating it

choices.label: C
choices.text: Palpating the abdomen during the speculum examination

choices.label: D
choices.text: Pressing suprapubically while the patient bears down

choices.label: E
choices.text: Stroking along the urethra from the anterior vagina

explanation.summary: In females, a stripping maneuver along the urethra from inside the anterior vagina reveals discharge.
explanation.whyCorrect: To evaluate the female urethra for discharge, a stripping maneuver is performed: a finger is inserted into the anterior vagina and stroked forward along the urethra. In males, the analogous maneuver is gentle stripping or milking of the penis.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Urination washes away discharge; it does not express it for inspection.
whyWrongByChoice.B: A cervical swab samples the cervix, not the urethra.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Abdominal palpation assesses pelvic tenderness, not urethral discharge.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Suprapubic pressure is not the described technique for expressing urethral discharge.

questions.topicName: Urethritis, Cervicitis, and Pelvic Inflammatory Disease

questions.stem: A 25-year-old man has had 3 weeks of mild dysuria as his only symptom. No discharge can be expressed even after gentle stripping of the penis. His partner was recently treated for a sexually transmitted infection. Which of the following organisms is most likely responsible?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Candida albicans

choices.label: B
choices.text: Chlamydia trachomatis

choices.label: C
choices.text: Neisseria gonorrhoeae

choices.label: D
choices.text: Staphylococcus saprophyticus

choices.label: E
choices.text: Streptococcus pyogenes

explanation.summary: Subacute urethritis with dysuria as the only symptom favors chlamydia over gonorrhea.
explanation.whyCorrect: Chlamydia is more likely than gonorrhea to be subacute or go undiagnosed. When dysuria is the only symptom, C. trachomatis infection is more likely than N. gonorrhoeae, which tends to produce an acute, purulent discharge.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Candida is a less common cause and is not suggested by this subacute STI picture with an affected partner.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Gonorrhea typically presents more acutely, often with frankly purulent discharge.
whyWrongByChoice.D: S. saprophyticus causes urinary tract infections, not sexually transmitted urethritis.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Streptococci are an uncommon cause and do not fit this partner-linked subacute presentation.

questions.topicName: Urethritis, Cervicitis, and Pelvic Inflammatory Disease

questions.stem: A 28-year-old man has urethritis. NAAT is negative for Neisseria gonorrhoeae and Chlamydia trachomatis, but an expanded NAAT panel identifies a bacterium that has been increasingly recognized as an important cause of urethritis and cervicitis. Which of the following organisms was most likely identified?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Listeria monocytogenes

choices.label: B
choices.text: Mycoplasma genitalium

choices.label: C
choices.text: Neisseria meningitidis

choices.label: D
choices.text: Proteus mirabilis

choices.label: E
choices.text: Staphylococcus saprophyticus

explanation.summary: M. genitalium is an increasingly recognized cause of urethritis and cervicitis and is detectable by NAAT.
explanation.whyCorrect: Beyond gonorrhea and chlamydia, other causes of urethritis and cervicitis include T. vaginalis, Candida, HSV, gram-negative facultative organisms, anaerobes, and streptococci. M. genitalium has more recently been recognized as an important cause, and NAAT can detect it.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Listeria is not a cause of urethritis or cervicitis.
whyWrongByChoice.C: N. meningitidis is not described as a cause of urethritis or cervicitis here.
whyWrongByChoice.D: P. mirabilis is an opportunistic organism in polymicrobial PID, not an emerging urethritis pathogen.
whyWrongByChoice.E: S. saprophyticus is a cause of cystitis, not an emerging STI cause of urethritis.

questions.topicName: Urethritis, Cervicitis, and Pelvic Inflammatory Disease

questions.stem: A 22-year-old sexually active woman has painful urination. Which of the following additional findings most favors a sexually transmitted urethritis over cystitis?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Discharge expressed from the meatus

choices.label: B
choices.text: Dysuria as her predominant complaint

choices.label: C
choices.text: Increased urinary frequency and urgency

choices.label: D
choices.text: Onset of symptoms shortly after intercourse

choices.label: E
choices.text: Urine culture growing Escherichia coli

explanation.summary: Urethral discharge points to STI urethritis; it is not typical of cystitis.
explanation.whyCorrect: Urethritis due to an STI is distinct from a UTI.
