Typical UTIs are caused by skin or GI flora such as E. coli and S. saprophyticus ascending into the bladder, and urethral discharge is not typically seen with them. Discharge expressed by stripping therefore favors urethritis.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Dysuria is common to both urethritis and cystitis.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Frequency occurs with bladder infection and is not specific for STI urethritis.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Recurrent cystitis in females can also be associated with sex because of the proximity of the anus, vagina, and urethra.
whyWrongByChoice.E: E. coli is the most common cause of cystitis, which favors a UTI.

questions.topicName: Urethritis, Cervicitis, and Pelvic Inflammatory Disease

questions.stem: A clinician considers ordering a Gram stain of cervical exudate for a woman with cervicitis. Which of the following limitations best explains why this test is seldom used today?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It cannot be performed on cervical swab material

choices.label: B
choices.text: It cannot visualize C. trachomatis or viruses

choices.label: C
choices.text: It is falsely positive from normal skin flora

choices.label: D
choices.text: It is invalid if collected during menstruation

choices.label: E
choices.text: It requires several days of incubation first

explanation.summary: Gram stain misses C. trachomatis and viruses and may be limited by insufficient sample.
explanation.whyCorrect: Gram stains are not commonly done for urethritis or cervicitis because many agents, such as C. trachomatis and viruses, cannot be visualized, and the sampled amount may be insufficient for detection.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Gram stain is performed on a swab of exudate material, including cervical samples.
whyWrongByChoice.C: False positives from skin flora are not the stated reason for disuse.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Menstruation is not the reason Gram stain has fallen out of use.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Incubation time is a drawback of culture, not Gram stain.

questions.topicName: Urethritis, Cervicitis, and Pelvic Inflammatory Disease

questions.stem: A 30-year-old man has gonococcal urethritis, and his clinician is concerned about possible antibiotic resistance. Which of the following tests allows determination of the organism's antibiotic susceptibility?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Bacterial culture of a urethral swab

choices.label: B
choices.text: Gram stain of urethral exudate

choices.label: C
choices.text: NAAT of a first-void urine sample

choices.label: D
choices.text: Serum complete blood count

choices.label: E
choices.text: Transrectal ultrasonography

explanation.summary: Culture, although time consuming, is the test that determines antibiotic susceptibility.
explanation.whyCorrect: Culture is slower than NAAT, but growing the organism allows determination of its antibiotic susceptibility.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Gram stain visualizes some organisms but gives no susceptibility data.
whyWrongByChoice.C: NAAT detects nucleic acid rapidly and sensitively but does not test antibiotic susceptibility.
whyWrongByChoice.D: A CBC may show leukocytosis but says nothing about the organism.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Imaging cannot assess the antibiotic susceptibility of a pathogen.

questions.topicName: Urethritis, Cervicitis, and Pelvic Inflammatory Disease

questions.stem: An 18-year-old woman has dysuria and mucopurulent cervical discharge, and gonorrhea or chlamydia is strongly suspected. NAAT results will take 4 days, and she says she is leaving town tomorrow and cannot return for follow-up. Which of the following is the most appropriate management?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Order a Gram stain and treat only if positive

choices.label: B
choices.text: Repeat NAAT in 2 weeks before deciding on therapy

choices.label: C
choices.text: Start empiric antibiotic treatment today

choices.label: D
choices.text: Treat only her sexual partner at this visit

choices.label: E
choices.text: Wait for NAAT results before giving any therapy

explanation.summary: Treat suspected gonorrhea or chlamydia empirically when reliable follow-up cannot be ensured.
explanation.whyCorrect: Prompt antimicrobial treatment reduces transmission and prevents ascending infection. Empiric treatment may be started when gonorrhea or chlamydia is strongly suspected, when testing is unavailable, or when reliable follow-up cannot be ensured, as here.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Gram stain cannot visualize C. trachomatis, so a negative result would not exclude infection.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Postponing treatment for 2 weeks risks ascending infection such as PID.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Partners should be evaluated and treated, but the patient herself also needs treatment.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Delaying treatment increases complications and transmission, and she cannot return for results.

questions.topicName: Urethritis, Cervicitis, and Pelvic Inflammatory Disease

questions.stem: A 27-year-old man has untreated gonococcal urethritis. Which of the following is a recognized complication of penile urethritis for which he is at risk?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Cystitis

choices.label: B
choices.text: Epididymitis

choices.label: C
choices.text: Hydronephrosis

choices.label: D
choices.text: Pyelonephritis

choices.label: E
choices.text: Salpingitis

explanation.summary: Complications of penile urethritis include orchitis, epididymitis, and prostatitis.
explanation.whyCorrect: Male upper reproductive tract infections, including orchitis, epididymitis, and prostatitis, are potential complications of penile urethritis, just as PID is a complication of cervicitis in females.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Cystitis is a urinary tract infection distinct from STI urethritis.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Hydronephrosis is not a complication of urethritis.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Pyelonephritis is an upper urinary tract infection by ascending gut or skin flora, not an STI complication.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Salpingitis is inflammation of the fallopian tubes, a component of PID in females.

questions.topicName: Urethritis, Cervicitis, and Pelvic Inflammatory Disease

questions.stem: During laparoscopy for suspected pelvic inflammatory disease, a surgeon sees swollen, erythematous fallopian tubes with purulent exudate. Which of the following terms describes this component of the disease?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Cervicitis

choices.label: B
choices.text: Endometritis

choices.label: C
choices.text: Oophoritis

choices.label: D
choices.text: Perihepatitis

choices.label: E
choices.text: Salpingitis

explanation.summary: PID includes endometritis (uterus), salpingitis (fallopian tubes), and oophoritis (ovaries).
explanation.whyCorrect: PID is inflammation of the female upper reproductive tract. Inflammation of the fallopian tubes is salpingitis; adhesions around the tubes from salpingitis are a major source of later chronic pelvic pain.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Cervicitis is a lower tract infection that usually precedes PID.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Endometritis is inflammation of the uterus.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Oophoritis is inflammation of the ovaries.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Perihepatitis is inflammation of the liver capsule (Fitz-Hugh-Curtis syndrome).

questions.topicName: Urethritis, Cervicitis, and Pelvic Inflammatory Disease

questions.stem: A 34-year-old woman in a long-term monogamous relationship develops fever, lower abdominal pain, and cervical motion tenderness 5 days after placement of an intrauterine device. NAAT for Neisseria gonorrhoeae and Chlamydia trachomatis is negative. Which of the following mechanisms best explains her infection?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Ascent of vaginal flora across the mucus barrier

choices.label: B
choices.text: Direct spread through the rectal wall

choices.label: C
choices.text: Hematogenous seeding from skin flora

choices.label: D
choices.text: Lymphatic spread from inguinal nodes

choices.label: E
choices.text: Reflux of infected urine into the uterus

explanation.summary: Not all PID is caused by STIs; procedures that breach the cervical mucus, such as IUD placement, can cause it.
explanation.whyCorrect: The cervix normally protects the sterile upper tract from vaginal organisms. PID can be caused by a procedure that breaches the cervical mucus, such as placement of an intrauterine device or an endometrial biopsy, allowing organisms to ascend.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Transmural spread from the rectum is not how procedure-related PID occurs.
whyWrongByChoice.C: PID arises from ascending spread through the cervix, not hematogenous seeding.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Inguinal lymphatic spread is not the route for PID.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Urinary reflux causes pyelonephritis, not upper genital tract infection.

questions.topicName: Urethritis, Cervicitis, and Pelvic Inflammatory Disease

questions.stem: A 22-year-old woman has lower abdominal pain and adnexal tenderness on bimanual examination. A vaginal speculum examination is then performed. Which of the following findings would most support a diagnosis of pelvic inflammatory disease?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A dilated os with tissue protruding through it

choices.label: B
choices.text: A painless, indurated ulcer on the labia

choices.label: C
choices.text: Erythematous, warm swelling of the vaginal wall

choices.label: D
choices.text: Purulent cervical discharge with friable tissue

choices.label: E
choices.text: Thin, clear mucus at a closed, pink cervical os

explanation.summary: Speculum exam in suspected PID looks for purulent cervical discharge and friability.
explanation.whyCorrect: Along with bimanual findings of lower abdominal, adnexal, and cervical motion tenderness, a speculum exam is performed to look for purulent cervical discharge and friability, which support PID.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Tissue at a dilated os is not a finding described for PID.
whyWrongByChoice.B: A genital ulcer suggests a pathogen other than gonorrhea or chlamydia and does not support PID.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Erythema, warmth, and swelling of the vaginal wall suggest vaginal cellulitis.
whyWrongByChoice.E: A normal-appearing cervix with clear mucus does not support PID.

questions.topicName: Urethritis, Cervicitis, and Pelvic Inflammatory Disease

questions.stem: A 25-year-old woman is clinically diagnosed with pelvic inflammatory disease based on history and bimanual findings. Her clinician orders transvaginal ultrasonography. Which of the following is the main purpose of this study?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Confirm mild PID with high sensitivity

choices.label: B
choices.text: Detect adhesions on the liver capsule

choices.label: C
choices.text: Identify the causative organism present

choices.label: D
choices.text: Measure the extent of peritoneal sepsis

choices.label: E
choices.text: Rule out a tubo-ovarian abscess

explanation.summary: Transvaginal ultrasonography is mainly used to rule out tubo-ovarian abscess or other causes of pain.
explanation.whyCorrect: Transvaginal ultrasonography may show thickened tubes, endometrial thickening, or ovarian cysts, but its sensitivity and specificity for PID are poor, especially in mild cases. It is mainly useful to rule out tubo-ovarian abscess or other causes of abdominopelvic pain.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Ultrasound has poor sensitivity for PID, especially mild disease.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Violin-string adhesions of Fitz-Hugh-Curtis syndrome are seen on laparoscopy.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Imaging cannot identify a pathogen; that requires NAAT, Gram stain, or culture.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Sepsis is a clinical diagnosis, not something ultrasound quantifies.

questions.topicName: Urethritis, Cervicitis, and Pelvic Inflammatory Disease

questions.stem: A 26-year-old woman is being treated for pelvic inflammatory disease. Her cervical NAAT is positive only for Chlamydia trachomatis, and no fluid from the uterus or fallopian tubes was sampled. Which of the following best describes the limitation of relying on her cervical result to define the pathogens?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It detects viral agents but not bacterial agents

choices.label: B
choices.text: It is less sensitive than Gram stain for chlamydia

choices.label: C
choices.text: It is unable to detect chlamydia in cervical samples

choices.label: D
choices.text: It overstates the number of organisms in the tubes

choices.label: E
choices.text: It reveals the inciting STI but misses ascending flora

explanation.summary: In PID, cervical swabs may show only the inciting STI, not the polymicrobial organisms that ascended.
explanation.whyCorrect: PID is usually a mixed infection in which opportunistic vaginal and GI organisms ascend through a compromised cervix. Urethral or cervical swabs may reveal only the inciting sexually transmitted organism, and infected fluid in the uterus and tubes is not easily accessible for sampling.

whyWrongByChoice.A: NAAT detects bacteria such as C. trachomatis and N. gonorrhoeae as well as viruses.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Gram stain cannot visualize C. trachomatis at all.
whyWrongByChoice.C: NAAT is highly sensitive for C. trachomatis in cervical samples.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The problem is underestimating, not overstating, the organisms in the upper tract.

questions.topicName: Urethritis, Cervicitis, and Pelvic Inflammatory Disease

questions.stem: A 32-year-old woman is evaluated for infertility. She had a chlamydial infection 6 years ago. On hysterosalpingography, dye fills the right fallopian tube and spills freely into the peritoneum, whereas the left tube is distended and no dye exits its end. Which of the following best describes the pathophysiology of the left-sided finding?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Distal tubal occlusion with trapped secretions

choices.label: B
choices.text: Implantation of an embryo within the tubal wall

choices.label: C
choices.text: Infection of the soft tissue of the vaginal wall

choices.label: D
choices.text: Inflammation of the fibrous capsule of the liver

choices.label: E
choices.text: Pus collecting within the tube and adjacent ovary

explanation.summary: Hydrosalpinx is distal tubal blockage with fluid accumulation, commonly after chlamydial or gonococcal PID.
explanation.whyCorrect: In hydrosalpinx the distal end of the fallopian tube becomes blocked, secretions accumulate, and the tube distends with fluid. On HSG, dye fails to spill from the affected tube. Prior PID or STI, especially chlamydia or gonorrhea, is a common cause, and hydrosalpinx is a well-recognized cause of infertility.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Ectopic pregnancy requires a pregnancy; she is being evaluated for infertility.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Vaginal cellulitis is a lower tract soft tissue infection unrelated to tubal patency.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Liver capsule inflammation is Fitz-Hugh-Curtis syndrome and would not change tubal dye flow.
whyWrongByChoice.E: A pus collection in tube and ovary is a tubo-ovarian abscess, an acute septic process.

questions.topicName: Urethritis, Cervicitis, and Pelvic Inflammatory Disease

questions.stem: A 23-year-old woman is hospitalized for pelvic inflammatory disease; ultrasonography on admission showed a complex pus-filled collection in the right adnexa. On hospital day 2 she suddenly develops diffuse abdominal pain, a rigid abdomen, and a blood pressure of 78/40 mm Hg. Which of the following is the most likely explanation?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Development of chronic pelvic pain

choices.label: B
choices.text: Formation of an ectopic pregnancy

choices.label: C
choices.text: Onset of Fitz-Hugh-Curtis perihepatitis

choices.label: D
choices.text: Progression to hydrosalpinx

choices.label: E
choices.text: Rupture with resultant peritonitis

explanation.summary: Rupture of a tubo-ovarian abscess can cause peritonitis, septic shock, and death.
explanation.whyCorrect: A tubo-ovarian abscess is a collection of pus in the tube, ovary, or uterus. It can rupture, leading to peritonitis, sepsis, and even death. Such patients may need drainage, and adnexectomy may be necessary in severe cases.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Chronic pelvic pain develops months to years later from scarring.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Ectopic pregnancy is a delayed complication and she has no pregnancy described.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Fitz-Hugh-Curtis causes pleuritic RUQ pain, not diffuse rigidity with shock.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Hydrosalpinx is a chronic tubal blockage, not an acute cause of shock.

questions.topicName: Urethritis, Cervicitis, and Pelvic Inflammatory Disease

questions.stem: A 29-year-old woman has vaginal pain 4 days after a vaginal delivery complicated by a laceration. She has a temperature of 38.3°C, and the vaginal wall is red, swollen, warm, and tender with purulent discharge. Bimanual examination shows no cervical motion or adnexal tenderness. Which of the following best characterizes her infection?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Ascending infection of the upper genital tract

choices.label: B
choices.text: Inflammation of the capsule around the liver

choices.label: C
choices.text: Localized soft tissue infection of the lower tract

choices.label: D
choices.text: Polymicrobial abscess of the tube and ovary

choices.label: E
choices.text: Sexually transmitted infection of the cervix

explanation.summary: Vaginal cellulitis is a localized soft tissue infection after a mucosal breach, unlike upper tract PID.
explanation.whyCorrect: Vaginal cellulitis is a bacterial infection of the soft tissues of the vaginal wall and nearby structures that usually follows mucosal disruption such as childbirth, procedures, trauma, or surgery. It presents with pain, erythema, swelling, warmth, tenderness, fever, and purulent discharge and is caused by organisms such as S. aureus, S. pyogenes, Group B Streptococcus, and anaerobes.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Upper tract infection (PID) would produce cervical motion or adnexal tenderness, which are absent.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Perihepatitis causes RUQ pain after PID, not local vaginal wall inflammation.
whyWrongByChoice.D: A tubo-ovarian abscess is an upper tract complication of PID with adnexal findings.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The picture follows delivery trauma and centers on the vaginal wall, not an STI of the cervix.

questions.topicName: Urethritis, Cervicitis, and Pelvic Inflammatory Disease

questions.stem: A 24-year-old man has nongonococcal urethritis confirmed by negative gonococcal NAAT; there is no indication for empiric gonococcal coverage. He says he rarely finishes multiday medication courses and will likely stop pills early. Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Azithromycin 1000 mg once

choices.label: B
choices.text: Ceftriaxone IM as a single dose

choices.label: C
choices.text: Doxycycline for 14 days

choices.label: D
choices.text: Doxycycline for 7 days

choices.label: E
choices.text: Metronidazole for 14 days

explanation.summary: Single-dose azithromycin 1000 mg is the alternative for nongonococcal urethritis when adherence is a concern.
explanation.whyCorrect: Nongonococcal urethritis or cervicitis without an indication for gonococcal coverage is treated with doxycycline for 7 days. Azithromycin as a single 1000 mg dose is the alternative when adherence to a multidose 7-day regimen is a substantial concern, as in this patient.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Ceftriaxone targets gonorrhea, which has been excluded.
whyWrongByChoice.C: A 14-day doxycycline course is part of PID therapy and worsens the adherence problem.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Doxycycline for 7 days is standard, but his expected nonadherence favors a single-dose option.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Metronidazole for 14 days belongs to the PID regimen.

questions.topicName: Urethritis, Cervicitis, and Pelvic Inflammatory Disease

questions.stem: A 29-year-old nonpregnant woman has cervicitis. NAAT is positive for Chlamydia trachomatis and negative for Neisseria gonorrhoeae. She is reliable and has completed multiday antibiotic courses before without difficulty. Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Azithromycin once plus metronidazole

choices.label: B
choices.text: Ceftriaxone IM as a single dose

choices.label: C
choices.text: Ceftriaxone IM plus doxycycline for 7 days

choices.label: D
choices.text: Doxycycline and metronidazole for 14 days

choices.label: E
choices.text: Doxycycline for 7 days

explanation.summary: Nongonococcal cervicitis without an indication for gonococcal coverage is treated with doxycycline for 7 days.
explanation.whyCorrect: With gonorrhea excluded and no indication for empiric gonococcal coverage, the recommended therapy for nongonococcal urethritis or cervicitis is doxycycline for 7 days. She is not pregnant and adherence is not a concern, so no alternative is needed.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Metronidazole adds anaerobic coverage needed in PID, not in chlamydial cervicitis.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Ceftriaxone alone treats gonorrhea and would leave her chlamydia untreated.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Adding ceftriaxone is unnecessary once gonorrhea has been excluded.
whyWrongByChoice.D: A 14-day doxycycline-metronidazole course is for PID, which she does not have.

questions.topicName: Urethritis, Cervicitis, and Pelvic Inflammatory Disease

questions.stem: A 27-year-old woman was admitted with severe pelvic inflammatory disease and started on parenteral antibiotics. By hospital day 3 she is afebrile, eating, and her pelvic tenderness has markedly improved. Which of the following is the most appropriate plan for the remainder of her therapy?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Discharge home with all antibiotics stopped

choices.label: B
choices.text: One oral azithromycin dose, then stop

choices.label: C
choices.text: Oral doxycycline alone for 7 more days

choices.label: D
choices.text: Oral doxycycline and metronidazole to day 14

choices.label: E
choices.text: Parenteral therapy for all 14 days

explanation.summary: After clinical improvement on parenteral therapy, oral doxycycline and metronidazole complete 14 days total.
explanation.whyCorrect: Hospitalized PID patients receive parenteral therapy; after clinical improvement, oral doxycycline and metronidazole are continued to complete a total of 14 days of therapy, maintaining coverage of chlamydia and anaerobic flora.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Stopping early risks relapse and long-term complications such as infertility.
whyWrongByChoice.B: A single azithromycin dose lacks anaerobic coverage and is far too short for PID.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Doxycycline alone omits anaerobic coverage needed for polymicrobial PID.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Parenteral therapy need not continue after improvement; an oral step-down is used.

questions.topicName: Urethritis, Cervicitis, and Pelvic Inflammatory Disease

questions.stem: A 26-year-old man receives ceftriaxone and a 7-day doxycycline prescription for gonococcal urethritis. His partner has been referred but not yet evaluated. He asks when he can safely resume sexual activity. Which of the following is the most appropriate advice?

choices.label: A
choices.text: After a single negative repeat urine NAAT of his own

choices.label: B
choices.text: As soon as he has received the ceftriaxone injection

choices.label: C
choices.text: Once his partner has one negative NAAT, even untreated

choices.label: D
choices.text: Twenty-four hours after the urethral discharge has stopped

choices.label: E
choices.text: When therapy ends, symptoms clear, and partner is treated

explanation.summary: Abstain until treatment is complete, symptoms resolve, and partners have been treated.
explanation.whyCorrect: Sex partners should be evaluated and treated. Patients should avoid sexual activity until treatment is complete, symptoms have resolved, and their partners have been treated, to reduce transmission and reinfection.

whyWrongByChoice.A: A negative test of his own ignores completion of therapy and partner treatment.
whyWrongByChoice.B: His doxycycline course is not complete and his partner is untreated.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Partners should be treated, not merely tested, before sexual activity resumes.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Resolution of discharge alone does not meet the criteria; therapy and partner treatment must be complete.

questions.topicName: Urethritis, Cervicitis, and Pelvic Inflammatory Disease

questions.stem: A 21-year-old woman has dysuria and a small amount of discharge expressed from the urethral meatus. She also reports a new, abnormal vaginal discharge. She has no abdominal or pelvic pain, and bimanual examination is nontender. The vaginal discharge most likely indicates which of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Ascending spread from the vagina into the tubes

choices.label: B
choices.text: Coexisting cystitis caused by Escherichia coli

choices.label: C
choices.text: Concurrent vaginitis from another infection

choices.label: D
choices.text: Early Fitz-Hugh-Curtis perihepatitis

choices.label: E
choices.text: Herpetic ulceration of the ectocervix

explanation.summary: Vaginal discharge in a patient with urethritis suggests concurrent vaginitis, since STIs often coexist with other infections.
explanation.whyCorrect: Symptoms of urethritis and cervicitis include dysuria, pruritus, and urethral discharge. Vaginal discharge is an indication of concurrent vaginitis, because STIs often cause other types of infection.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Ascending infection (PID) would cause lower abdominal pain and pelvic tenderness, which are absent.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Cystitis does not typically produce vaginal or urethral discharge.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Perihepatitis causes RUQ pain as a complication of PID, not vaginal discharge.
whyWrongByChoice.E: No genital ulcers are described; ulcers would prompt a search for HSV.

questions.topicName: Urethritis, Cervicitis, and Pelvic Inflammatory Disease

questions.stem: A 25-year-old woman who was treated for pelvic inflammatory disease 2 years ago asks how likely it is that the infection will affect her ability to conceive. Among women with a history of pelvic inflammatory disease, approximately what proportion will have trouble getting pregnant?

choices.label: A
choices.text: One in eight

choices.label: B
choices.text: One in four

choices.label: C
choices.text: One in one hundred

choices.label: D
choices.text: One in twenty

choices.label: E
choices.text: One in two

explanation.summary: About one in eight women with a history of PID will have trouble getting pregnant.
explanation.whyCorrect: PID can permanently damage the reproductive organs, and among those with a history of PID, one in eight will have trouble getting pregnant. Tubal scarring, adhesions from salpingitis, and hydrosalpinx contribute to this infertility.

whyWrongByChoice.B: One in four overstates the stated risk of one in eight.
whyWrongByChoice.C: One in one hundred greatly understates the risk.
whyWrongByChoice.D: One in twenty understates the stated risk of one in eight.
whyWrongByChoice.E: One in two greatly overstates the infertility risk after PID.

questions.topicName: Urethritis, Cervicitis, and Pelvic Inflammatory Disease

questions.stem: A 30-year-old woman with a history of pelvic inflammatory disease has 7 weeks of amenorrhea, light spotting, and unilateral pelvic pain. A urine pregnancy test is positive, and no intrauterine pregnancy is seen on ultrasonography. Which of the following long-term complications of her prior infection is most likely present?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Chronic epididymitis

choices.label: B
choices.text: Ectopic pregnancy

choices.label: C
choices.text: Fitz-Hugh-Curtis syndrome

choices.label: D
choices.text: Recurrent cervicitis

choices.label: E
choices.text: Vaginal cellulitis

explanation.summary: Tubal scarring after PID raises the risk of ectopic pregnancy.
explanation.whyCorrect: Complications of PID can occur months to years later and include infertility, ectopic pregnancy, and chronic pelvic pain from scarring, especially adhesions around the fallopian tubes from salpingitis. A positive pregnancy test without an intrauterine pregnancy in this setting indicates ectopic pregnancy.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Epididymitis is a male complication of urethritis.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Fitz-Hugh-Curtis causes RUQ pain with breathing and does not explain a positive pregnancy test.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Recurrent cervicitis would not explain a positive pregnancy test without an intrauterine pregnancy.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Vaginal cellulitis is a local soft tissue infection after mucosal disruption, not a PID sequela.

questions.topicName: Urethritis, Cervicitis, and Pelvic Inflammatory Disease

questions.stem: A 27-year-old man comes to the emergency department 2 hours after abrupt onset of severe left scrotal pain that woke him from sleep. He is afebrile and has no dysuria or urethral discharge. The left testis is exquisitely tender, and stroking the inner thigh produces no retraction of the left testis. Color Doppler ultrasonography shows diminished flow to the left testis. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Acute bacterial epididymitis

choices.label: B
choices.text: Autoimmune orchitis

choices.label: C
choices.text: Epididymo-orchitis

choices.label: D
choices.text: Mumps orchitis

choices.label: E
choices.text: Testicular torsion

explanation.summary: Sudden severe pain, no fever, an absent cremasteric reflex and reduced blood flow point to torsion, the most time-sensitive cause of acute scrotal pain.
explanation.whyCorrect: Torsion is of sudden onset with severe pain, reduced testicular blood flow and typically no fever, and the cremasteric reflex is frequently absent. It is the first diagnosis to exclude in acute scrotal pain because it must be identified quickly and treated surgically.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Epididymitis develops gradually, often with dysuria or discharge, has an intact cremasteric reflex and shows hyperemia on Doppler.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Autoimmune orchitis is a rare noninfectious inflammation causing impaired spermatogenesis, not an abrupt vascular emergency with lost flow.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Epididymo-orchitis is inflammatory, with increased blood flow and an intact cremasteric reflex.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Mumps orchitis is of gradual onset, often follows parotitis, keeps the cremasteric reflex intact and shows increased (not reduced) blood flow.

questions.stem: A 19-year-old college student has had painful swelling of both cheeks just in front of the ears for 5 days. He now reports progressive right testicular pain. He has no record of childhood immunizations. He is sexually inactive. Examination shows diffuse swelling and exquisite tenderness of the right testis; the cremasteric reflex is intact. Urinalysis is normal. Which of the following is the most likely cause of his testicular findings?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Chlamydia trachomatis

choices.label: B
choices.text: Coxsackie B virus

choices.label: C
choices.text: Escherichia coli

choices.label: D
choices.text: Mumps orthorubulavirus

choices.label: E
choices.text: Neisseria gonorrhoeae

explanation.summary: Isolated orchitis in an unvaccinated postpubertal male after parotitis is mumps orchitis.
explanation.whyCorrect: Isolated orchitis is primarily viral and specifically due to mumps; lack of MMR vaccination is the dominant risk factor. Orchitis typically follows parotitis by 4-6 days, is most likely after puberty, and leaves urinalysis normal because spread is hematogenous.

whyWrongByChoice.A: C. trachomatis causes STI-associated epididymo-orchitis with urethritis and pyuria, not orchitis after parotitis in a sexually inactive man.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Coxsackie B is a rare cause of viral orchitis and is not associated with preceding parotitis.
whyWrongByChoice.C: E. coli causes epididymitis tied to urinary infection or urologic disease, with abnormal urinalysis.
whyWrongByChoice.E: N. gonorrhoeae causes epididymo-orchitis via urethritis; urinalysis would typically show pyuria.

questions.stem: A 23-year-old man has had dysuria and a thin urethral discharge for 10 days. Over the past 3 days he has developed gradually worsening pain behind the left testis. He has had several new sexual partners this year. Temperature is 37.9 C. There is focal tenderness over the posterior epididymis and a thickened spermatic cord; the cremasteric reflex is present. Which of the following organisms is the most likely cause?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Chlamydia trachomatis

choices.label: B
choices.text: Escherichia coli

choices.label: C
choices.text: Mumps orthorubulavirus

choices.label: D
choices.text: Mycobacterium tuberculosis

choices.label: E
choices.text: Pseudomonas aeruginosa

explanation.summary: Epididymitis in men under 35 is usually an STI complication, most often C. trachomatis or N. gonorrhoeae.
explanation.whyCorrect: Epididymitis in adolescents and younger men is usually due to STI, most often C. trachomatis and N. gonorrhoeae, spreading from urethritis to the epididymis. Urethral discharge and dysuria preceding gradual posterior testicular pain fit this ascending pattern.

whyWrongByChoice.B: E. coli is the typical cause in boys with UTI and in older men with urologic disease, not a young man with urethritis and new partners.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Mumps causes orchitis after parotitis via hematogenous spread, not urethral discharge with epididymal tenderness.
whyWrongByChoice.D: M. tuberculosis is an uncommon cause, seen especially in HIV-positive patients.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Pseudomonas is a cause in older men, particularly with urinary stasis or instrumentation.

questions.stem: A 71-year-old man with benign prostatic hypertrophy had an indwelling urethral catheter placed during a hospitalization 1 week ago. He now has 3 days of gradually worsening right scrotal pain and a temperature of 38.4 C. He has been in a monogamous marriage for 45 years. The right scrotum is warm, erythematous and tender posteriorly. Urinalysis shows pyuria. Which of the following is the most likely causative organism?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Chlamydia trachomatis

choices.label: B
choices.text: Escherichia coli

choices.label: C
choices.text: Mumps orthorubulavirus

choices.label: D
choices.text: Neisseria gonorrhoeae

choices.label: E
choices.text: Treponema pallidum

explanation.summary: In men 35 and older, epididymitis usually stems from urologic conditions and is caused by coliforms such as E. coli.
explanation.whyCorrect: In older men, epididymitis is commonly due to BPH with urinary stasis, urinary tract infection or catheterization, and the organisms are E. coli, other gram-negative bacteria and gram-positive cocci. His catheter, BPH and low STI risk all point to a urinary pathogen.

whyWrongByChoice.A: C. trachomatis predominates in sexually active men under 35; this man has low STI risk and an instrumentation history.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Mumps is a cause of orchitis in unvaccinated postpubertal males, not catheter-associated epididymitis with pyuria.
whyWrongByChoice.D: N. gonorrhoeae is an STI cause typical of younger men, not a catheterized older man in a long monogamous marriage.
whyWrongByChoice.E: T. pallidum is a less common cause of epididymitis seen as part of syphilis.

questions.stem: A 26-year-old man has 4 days of dysuria, purulent urethral discharge and gradually increasing pain over the posterior aspect of the left testis. The cremasteric reflex is intact and Doppler shows increased epididymal flow. A first-void urine NAAT is sent. Which of the following is the most appropriate empiric management while results are pending?

choices.label: A
choices.text: IM ceftriaxone as a single agent

choices.label: B
choices.text: IM ceftriaxone plus oral doxycycline

choices.label: C
choices.text: NSAIDs, ice and scrotal elevation only

choices.label: D
choices.text: Oral levofloxacin alone

choices.label: E
choices.text: Oral trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole alone

explanation.summary: Suspected STI-related epididymitis is treated with ceftriaxone (gonorrhea) plus doxycycline (chlamydia).
explanation.whyCorrect: When an STI is suspected, oral doxycycline and IM or IV ceftriaxone should be given. Ceftriaxone covers N. gonorrhoeae and doxycycline covers C. trachomatis, the two most common causes in men under 35; NSAIDs and scrotal support can be added for symptoms.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Ceftriaxone alone covers N. gonorrhoeae but leaves C. trachomatis untreated.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Supportive care alone is appropriate for mumps orchitis, not bacterial epididymitis.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Levofloxacin is chosen for men 35 and older at low STI risk to cover urinary pathogens.
whyWrongByChoice.E: TMP-SMX targets urinary-associated bacteria in low-STI-risk older men, not gonorrhea and chlamydia.

questions.stem: A 64-year-old man with benign prostatic hypertrophy and urinary hesitancy has 4 days of gradually worsening left scrotal pain. He has had one sexual partner, his wife, for 38 years. The left epididymis is swollen and tender; the cremasteric reflex is intact. Urinalysis shows leukocyte esterase and pyuria. NAAT for C. trachomatis and N. gonorrhoeae is negative. Which of the following is the most appropriate antibiotic therapy?

choices.label: A
choices.text: IM ceftriaxone alone

choices.label: B
choices.text: IM ceftriaxone plus oral doxycycline

choices.label: C
choices.text: No antibiotics; supportive care only

choices.label: D
choices.text: Oral doxycycline alone

choices.label: E
choices.text: Oral levofloxacin

explanation.summary: Men 35 and older at low STI risk receive levofloxacin or TMP-SMX to cover urinary pathogens.
explanation.whyCorrect: For men aged 35 and older at low risk for STIs, typical treatment is oral levofloxacin or trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole, both of which cover urinary-associated bacteria such as E. coli. His BPH, pyuria and negative NAAT fit a urinary source.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Ceftriaxone is included to cover N. gonorrhoeae in STI-related disease.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Ceftriaxone plus doxycycline targets gonorrhea and chlamydia, the regimen for suspected STI.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Supportive care alone is for viral (mumps) orchitis; bacterial epididymitis requires antibiotics.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Doxycycline alone covers chlamydia, which is unlikely here, and is not the urinary-pathogen choice.

questions.stem: A 17-year-old unvaccinated boy developed parotid swelling 6 days ago and now has painful swelling of the left testis. RT-PCR of a buccal swab confirms mumps. Urinalysis is normal and Doppler shows testicular hyperemia. Which of the following is the most appropriate management?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Emergent scrotal surgical exploration

choices.label: B
choices.text: IM ceftriaxone plus oral doxycycline

choices.label: C
choices.text: NSAIDs, ice, scrotal elevation and rest

choices.label: D
choices.text: Oral levofloxacin for urinary pathogens

choices.label: E
choices.text: Oral trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole course

explanation.summary: Mumps orchitis is viral, so treatment is supportive rather than antibiotic-based.
explanation.whyCorrect: When mumps is the cause, treatment is supportive: analgesics (NSAIDs), ice, scrotal elevation and rest. Antibiotics do not treat a viral infection; prevention depends on MMR vaccination.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Surgical exploration is for torsion; hyperemia on Doppler and confirmed mumps argue against it.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Ceftriaxone plus doxycycline covers gonorrhea and chlamydia and has no role in viral orchitis.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Levofloxacin covers urinary bacteria in older low-STI-risk men and does not treat mumps.
whyWrongByChoice.E: TMP-SMX is an alternative for bacterial epididymitis from urinary pathogens, not viral orchitis.

questions.stem: A 30-year-old man has 3 days of gradually worsening right scrotal pain with dysuria. The right hemiscrotum is warm and erythematous. Which of the following examination findings would best support epididymitis over testicular torsion?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Diffuse scrotal tenderness on palpation

choices.label: B
choices.text: Mild erythema of the scrotal skin

choices.label: C
choices.text: Pain relief when the testis is lifted

choices.label: D
choices.text: Testis retracts when the inner thigh is stroked

choices.label: E
choices.text: Tightness of the scrotum with a drawn-up testis

explanation.summary: An intact cremasteric reflex supports epididymitis; the reflex is frequently absent in torsion.
explanation.whyCorrect: The cremasteric reflex, retraction of the testis on stroking the inner thigh, is intact in epididymitis, orchitis and epididymo-orchitis but frequently absent in torsion, so examining it helps distinguish them.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Tenderness is present in both inflammatory conditions and torsion and does not separate them.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Scrotal erythema can accompany several causes of scrotal pain and is not discriminating.
whyWrongByChoice.C: A positive Prehn sign may occur in epididymitis but is not specific and is seen in other testicular disorders.
whyWrongByChoice.E: A tight scrotum with a drawn-up testis can be seen in epididymitis and does not reliably exclude torsion.

questions.stem: A 22-year-old man presents with gradual-onset posterior testicular pain, dysuria and scant urethral discharge. The physician wants the most accurate test for C. trachomatis and N. gonorrhoeae. Which of the following specimens and methods is most appropriate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Blood culture drawn before antibiotics

choices.label: B
choices.text: Culture of a midstream urine specimen

choices.label: C
choices.text: NAAT of a first-void urine specimen

choices.label: D
choices.text: NAAT of a urethral swab specimen

choices.label: E
choices.text: RT-PCR of a saliva specimen

explanation.summary: NAAT on first-void urine is the more accurate specimen for chlamydia and gonorrhea.
explanation.whyCorrect: NAAT can be performed on first-void urine or a urethral swab, and first-void urine is the more accurate specimen. It detects C. trachomatis and N. gonorrhoeae and is helpful in symptomatic men under 35 or at STI risk.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Blood cultures are indicated only if the patient has a fever and do not detect chlamydia.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Routine urine culture is positive in only about a quarter of epididymitis cases and does not detect chlamydia.
whyWrongByChoice.D: A urethral swab NAAT is acceptable but less accurate than first-void urine.
whyWrongByChoice.E: RT-PCR of saliva or buccal swab is used to diagnose mumps, not STIs.

questions.stem: A 20-year-old man with confirmed mumps has painful swelling of the right testis. Urinalysis shows no leukocytes, negative leukocyte esterase and no bacteria. Which of the following best explains the urinalysis findings?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Infection ascends via the vas deferens, bypassing the bladder

choices.label: B
choices.text: Mumps virus suppresses neutrophil entry into the urine

choices.label: C
choices.text: Orchitis precedes urethral involvement by several weeks

choices.label: D
choices.text: Parotid inflammation sequesters circulating leukocytes

choices.label: E
choices.text: Viral spread is hematogenous rather than ascending

explanation.summary: Mumps orchitis follows hematogenous spread, so there is no urethritis, pyuria or bacteriuria.
explanation.whyCorrect: Mumps-related orchitis results from hematogenous spread of the virus, not ascending infection. Because the urinary tract is not involved, there is typically no urethritis, no pyuria and no bacteriuria, so urinalysis in isolated orchitis is usually normal.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Ascending spread through the vas deferens is the route of bacterial epididymitis, which typically produces pyuria.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The normal urinalysis reflects the route of infection, not viral suppression of leukocytes.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Mumps orchitis does not later progress to urethral infection; the urinary tract is not involved.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Parotitis does not explain the absence of pyuria; the urinary tract is simply not infected.

questions.stem: A 28-year-old man had mumps orchitis affecting both testes 2 years ago. He and his partner are planning a pregnancy and ask about his fertility. Approximately what proportion of adult men with this history have reduced fertility?

explanation.summary: Bilateral mumps orchitis reduces fertility in about 65% of affected adult men (unilateral about 25%).
explanation.whyCorrect: Untreated orchitis may reduce fertility, especially with mumps. Unilateral and bilateral mumps orchitis reduce fertility in about 25% and 65% of affected adult males, respectively; this man had bilateral disease.

whyWrongByChoice.A: 5% underestimates the impact; even unilateral mumps orchitis affects about 25%.
whyWrongByChoice.B: About 25% applies to unilateral mumps orchitis, not bilateral disease.
whyWrongByChoice.C: 45% does not match the reported figure of about 65% for bilateral disease.
whyWrongByChoice.E: 85% overstates the proportion; bilateral mumps orchitis reduces fertility in about 65%.

questions.stem: A 29-year-old HIV-negative man who has sex with men as the insertive partner during anal intercourse has 5 days of worsening left scrotal pain and fever. He has no urinary catheter or recent instrumentation. NAAT of first-void urine is negative for C. trachomatis and N. gonorrhoeae. Which of the following is the most likely causative organism?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Coxsackie B virus

choices.label: B
choices.text: Enterobacter species

choices.label: C
choices.text: Mumps orthorubulavirus

choices.label: D
choices.text: Mycobacterium tuberculosis

choices.label: E
choices.text: Treponema pallidum

explanation.summary: Insertive anal intercourse predisposes to coliform epididymitis (Citrobacter, Enterobacter), which is destructive and abscess-prone.
explanation.whyCorrect: Besides chlamydia and gonorrhea, an important cause of epididymitis in sexually active men, especially insertive partners in anal intercourse, is fecal coliform bacteria such as Citrobacter and Enterobacter. These organisms are highly destructive and tend to form abscesses.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Coxsackie B is a rare cause of viral orchitis, not coliform-exposure epididymitis.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Mumps causes orchitis by hematogenous spread in unvaccinated males, typically after parotitis.
whyWrongByChoice.D: M. tuberculosis is an uncommon cause of epididymitis seen especially in HIV-positive patients.
whyWrongByChoice.E: T. pallidum is a less common cause of epididymitis occurring as part of syphilis; his exposure favors fecal organisms.

questions.stem: A 16-year-old unvaccinated boy developed bilateral parotid swelling 2 days ago and today has right testicular pain and swelling. Which of the following is the most appropriate test to confirm the suspected viral cause?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Blood cultures from two separate sites

choices.label: B
choices.text: Culture of a midstream urine specimen

choices.label: C
choices.text: NAAT of a first-void urine specimen

choices.label: D
choices.text: RT-PCR of a buccal swab specimen

choices.label: E
choices.text: Serology repeated in convalescence

explanation.summary: Mumps is diagnosed early by RT-PCR of saliva or a buccal swab.
explanation.whyCorrect: Mumps is diagnosed by RT-PCR of saliva or buccal swab, particularly early in disease. NAAT of urine or urethral swab is not recommended for mumps, and serology is reserved for late disease or convalescence.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Blood cultures are for febrile patients with suspected bacterial infection and do not identify mumps.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Urine culture seeks bacteria and would be expected to be negative in mumps orchitis.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Urine NAAT detects chlamydia and gonorrhea and is not recommended for mumps.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Serology is used late in disease or in convalescence; this boy is early in his illness.

questions.stem: A 24-year-old man who received two doses of MMR vaccine in childhood had parotitis followed by left testicular swelling 3 weeks ago during a campus outbreak. No early testing was done. Serologic testing now in convalescence is negative. Which of the following best explains why this result does not exclude mumps?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Mumps orchitis produces no antibody response at all

choices.label: B
choices.text: Mumps should be diagnosed by urine NAAT instead

choices.label: C
choices.text: Parotid inflammation consumes circulating antibody

choices.label: D
choices.text: Serology is less sensitive in vaccinated persons

choices.label: E
choices.text: Serology is valid only in the first 48 hours

explanation.summary: Mumps serology is used late in disease but is less sensitive in vaccinated individuals.
explanation.whyCorrect: Serology may be used for diagnosis late in disease or in convalescence, but it is less sensitive in vaccinated individuals, so a negative result in a vaccinated man does not rule out mumps. RT-PCR of saliva or buccal swab is preferred early in disease.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Serology can detect mumps; the issue is reduced sensitivity after vaccination.
whyWrongByChoice.B: NAAT of urine or urethral swab is not recommended for mumps.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Parotitis does not consume antibody; the limitation is vaccination status.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Serology is the late-disease and convalescent test; early disease favors RT-PCR.

questions.stem: An 8-year-old unvaccinated boy is diagnosed with mumps during a community outbreak. Which of the following is the most common clinical manifestation of this infection?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Epididymitis

choices.label: B
choices.text: Meningitis

choices.label: C
choices.text: Orchitis

choices.label: D
choices.text: Pancreatitis

choices.label: E
choices.text: Parotitis

explanation.summary: Parotitis is the most common manifestation of mumps.
explanation.whyCorrect: The most common clinical manifestation of mumps is parotitis, painful swelling of the parotid glands. Meningitis, orchitis and pancreatitis are complications.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Mumps is a less common cause of epididymitis, usually when epididymo-orchitis is present.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Meningitis is a recognized complication, not the most common manifestation.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Orchitis is a complication, mostly after puberty, affecting about 20-30% of postpubertal males with mumps.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Pancreatitis is a complication of mumps rather than its usual presentation.

questions.stem: During a mumps outbreak among unvaccinated adults, health officials counsel infected men about testicular complications. Approximately what proportion of postpubertal males with mumps develop orchitis?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Fewer than 1%

choices.label: B
choices.text: About 5%

choices.label: C
choices.text: About 20-30%

choices.label: D
choices.text: About 50-60%

choices.label: E
choices.text: About 75%

explanation.summary: Mumps orchitis develops in roughly 20-30% of postpubertal males with mumps.
explanation.whyCorrect: Mumps orchitis develops in approximately 20-30% of postpubertal males with mumps. Although mumps is most common in children, orchitis is most likely after puberty, and lack of MMR vaccination is the dominant risk factor.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Fewer than 1% far underestimates orchitis in postpubertal males with mumps.
whyWrongByChoice.B: About 5% is too low; the figure is about 20-30%.
whyWrongByChoice.D: 50-60% overestimates the incidence of mumps orchitis.
whyWrongByChoice.E: 75% greatly overstates how often orchitis complicates mumps.

questions.stem: A physician compares viral orchitis with bacterial epididymo-orchitis. Which of the following features is more characteristic of viral orchitis than of the other causes of orchitis?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Involvement of both testes in about 30% of cases

choices.label: B
choices.text: Onset following urethral catheterization

choices.label: C
choices.text: Positive urine culture for gram-negative rods

choices.label: D
choices.text: Purulent urethral discharge preceding pain

choices.label: E
choices.text: Tendency toward abscess formation

explanation.summary: A significant portion (~30%) of viral orchitis is bilateral, unlike other causes.
explanation.whyCorrect: Unlike other causes of orchitis, a significant portion of viral orchitis cases (about 30%) affect both testicles, often as part of an overall viral syndrome. Viral orchitis spreads hematogenously, so urinary findings are typically absent.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Catheterization predisposes older men to bacterial epididymitis.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Gram-negative urinary infection is typical of bacterial disease in boys and older men.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Urethral discharge reflects STI urethritis leading to bacterial epididymo-orchitis.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Abscess formation is characteristic of coliform epididymitis, as in insertive anal intercourse.

questions.stem: A 14-year-old boy who is fully vaccinated with MMR has fever, malaise and myalgias followed by painful swelling of one testis. RT-PCR for mumps is negative. Urinalysis is normal. Which of the following is the most likely cause?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Chlamydia trachomatis

choices.label: B
choices.text: Coxsackie B virus

choices.label: C
choices.text: Mycobacterium tuberculosis

choices.label: D
choices.text: Pseudomonas aeruginosa

choices.label: E
choices.text: Treponema pallidum

explanation.summary: Besides mumps, orchitis is rarely caused by other viruses such as coxsackie B.
explanation.whyCorrect: Orchitis in children and teens is typically part of an overall viral syndrome. Mumps is the classic cause, but orchitis is rarely caused by other viruses such as coxsackie B virus, which fits a vaccinated boy with negative mumps testing.

whyWrongByChoice.A: C. trachomatis causes STI-associated epididymo-orchitis with urethritis and abnormal urinalysis.
whyWrongByChoice.C: M. tuberculosis is an uncommon cause of epididymitis, especially in HIV-positive patients.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Pseudomonas causes epididymo-orchitis in older men with urologic conditions.
whyWrongByChoice.E: T. pallidum is an uncommon cause of epididymitis as part of syphilis, not a viral syndrome.

questions.stem: A 32-year-old man is evaluated for infertility. Semen analysis shows a markedly reduced count. Testicular biopsy shows granulomatous inflammation of the seminiferous tubules; stains and cultures show no organisms, and NAAT and mumps testing are negative. Which of the following best describes the mechanism of his condition?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Ascending coliform infection from the bladder

choices.label: B
choices.text: Hematogenous seeding of the testis by mumps virus

choices.label: C
choices.text: Immune attack on sperm antigens after barrier breach

choices.label: D
choices.text: Reactivation of latent Mycobacterium tuberculosis

choices.label: E
choices.text: Reflux of urine into the epididymis during straining

explanation.summary: Autoimmune orchitis follows blood-testis barrier disruption, exposing sperm antigens to the immune system.
explanation.whyCorrect: Autoimmune orchitis is a rare noninfectious inflammation caused by immune exposure to sperm antigens after disruption of the blood-testis barrier. It may be lymphocytic or granulomatous, involves the seminiferous tubules, is often associated with anti-sperm antibodies, and impairs spermatogenesis, causing infertility.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Ascending coliform infection causes bacterial epididymitis with positive cultures or pyuria.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Mumps orchitis is infectious and testing here was negative.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Tuberculous epididymitis is infectious; stains and cultures showed no organisms.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Urinary reflux during straining is a noninfectious cause of epididymitis, not granulomatous tubular orchitis.

questions.stem: A 34-year-old man with acute scrotal pain reports that his pain lessens when the examiner gently lifts the affected testis. Which of the following is the most accurate interpretation of this finding?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It confirms testicular torsion

choices.label: B
choices.text: It excludes bacterial epididymitis

choices.label: C
choices.text: It is nonspecific for any one disorder

choices.label: D
choices.text: It proves isolated viral orchitis

choices.label: E
choices.text: It reflects an absent cremasteric reflex

explanation.summary: A positive Prehn sign may occur in orchitis and epididymitis but is not specific.
explanation.whyCorrect: The Prehn sign is pain relief with scrotal elevation. It may be positive in orchitis, epididymitis and epididymo-orchitis, but it is not specific and can be seen in other testicular disorders, so it cannot establish the diagnosis on its own.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The Prehn sign does not confirm torsion; the cremasteric reflex and Doppler flow are more helpful.
whyWrongByChoice.B: A positive Prehn sign is compatible with epididymitis rather than excluding it.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The sign can occur with several conditions and does not prove viral orchitis.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The Prehn sign and cremasteric reflex are separate findings; the reflex is intact in epididymitis and orchitis.

questions.stem: Which of the following correctly describes the location and function of the epididymis?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Anterior to the testis; carries sperm to the prostate

choices.label: B
choices.text: Behind the testis; carries sperm to the ductus deferens

choices.label: C
choices.text: Inside the testis; forms sperm within its tubules

choices.label: D
choices.text: Lateral to the testis; carries urine to the urethra

choices.label: E
choices.text: Within the spermatic cord; carries sperm to the bladder

explanation.summary: The epididymis is the duct behind the testis that passes sperm to the ductus (vas) deferens.
explanation.whyCorrect: The epididymis is the duct behind the testis that allows sperm to pass from the testis to the ductus deferens (vas deferens). This is why epididymitis pain and tenderness localize to the posterior aspect of the testis.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The epididymis lies posterior, not anterior, and drains into the ductus deferens.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Sperm are produced in the seminiferous tubules of the testis, not the epididymis.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The epididymis carries sperm, not urine.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The epididymis does not lie within the spermatic cord or drain to the bladder.

questions.stem: Among adult men presenting to outpatient care with scrotal pain, which of the following is the most common cause?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Autoimmune orchitis

choices.label: B
choices.text: Coxsackie B orchitis

choices.label: C
choices.text: Epididymitis

choices.label: D
choices.text: Isolated mumps orchitis

choices.label: E
choices.text: Testicular torsion

explanation.summary: Epididymitis is the most common cause of scrotal pain in adults.
explanation.whyCorrect: Epididymitis, usually a complication of STI urethritis, is the most common cause of scrotal pain in adults. Torsion must be excluded first because it is time-sensitive, but it is less common.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Autoimmune orchitis is rare.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Coxsackie B is a rare cause of orchitis.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Mumps orchitis is now uncommon in the United States due to MMR vaccination.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Torsion is the most time-sensitive diagnosis, not the most common one in adults.

questions.stem: A 6-year-old boy has 2 days of fever, dysuria and increasing left scrotal pain. The left epididymis is swollen and tender, and the cremasteric reflex is present. Urinalysis shows pyuria and bacteriuria. Which of the following is the most likely causative organism?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Chlamydia trachomatis

choices.label: B
choices.text: Escherichia coli

choices.label: C
choices.text: Mumps orthorubulavirus

choices.label: D
choices.text: Neisseria gonorrhoeae

choices.label: E
choices.text: Treponema pallidum

explanation.summary: Epididymitis in boys is almost always associated with UTI caused by E. coli or other gram-negatives.
explanation.whyCorrect: Epididymitis can occur in children. In boys it is almost always associated with a urinary tract infection, with E. coli (and less often other gram-negative organisms) as the cause, consistent with his pyuria and bacteriuria.

whyWrongByChoice.A: C. trachomatis is an STI cause in adolescents and young men, not young boys.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Mumps causes orchitis by hematogenous spread with a normal urinalysis.
whyWrongByChoice.D: N. gonorrhoeae is likewise an STI cause in sexually active adolescents and young men.
whyWrongByChoice.E: T. pallidum is an uncommon cause of epididymitis as part of syphilis.

questions.stem: A 35-year-old man became infertile after bilateral mumps orchitis; semen analysis shows almost no sperm. A fertility specialist proposes retrieving occasional spermatozoa by testicular biopsy for intracytoplasmic sperm injection. Which of the following concerns about this approach should be discussed?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Inability to fertilize with biopsy-derived sperm

choices.label: B
choices.text: More chromosomal anomalies and childhood cancers

choices.label: C
choices.text: Need for MMR revaccination before sperm retrieval

choices.label: D
choices.text: Recurrence of orchitis triggered by the biopsy

choices.label: E
choices.text: Transmission of mumps virus to the embryo

explanation.summary: Sperm retrieval by testicular biopsy for ICSI raises concerns about chromosomal abnormalities and childhood cancers in offspring.
explanation.whyCorrect: For infertile men, assisted reproductive technologies can retrieve occasional spermatozoa by testicular biopsy for intracytoplasmic sperm injection. There are concerns about increased incidence of chromosomal abnormalities and childhood cancers among children conceived this way.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Biopsy-retrieved spermatozoa are used successfully for ICSI; that is the purpose of the technique.
whyWrongByChoice.C: MMR prevents mumps infection; revaccination is not a prerequisite for sperm retrieval.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Biopsy-triggered recurrence of orchitis is not the recognized concern.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Transmission of mumps virus to the embryo is not the concern raised about this approach.

questions.stem: A 38-year-old HIV-positive man with a low CD4 count has several weeks of left scrotal swelling and discomfort. First-void urine NAAT for C. trachomatis and N. gonorrhoeae is negative, and routine urine culture is negative. He has no history of urinary instrumentation. Which of the following less common causes of epididymitis is most strongly associated with his underlying condition?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Coxsackie B virus

choices.label: B
choices.text: Enterobacter species

choices.label: C
choices.text: Escherichia coli

choices.label: D
choices.text: Mumps orthorubulavirus

choices.label: E
choices.text: Mycobacterium tuberculosis

explanation.summary: Mycobacterium tuberculosis is a less common cause of epididymitis, seen especially in HIV-positive patients.
explanation.whyCorrect: Less common infectious causes of epididymitis include mumps, Mycobacterium tuberculosis (especially in HIV-positive patients), Treponema pallidum and fungal organisms. His HIV status with negative STI testing and routine culture points toward tuberculosis.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Coxsackie B is a rare viral cause of orchitis, not specifically linked to HIV.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Enterobacter is a coliform cause tied to insertive anal intercourse and would grow on routine culture.
whyWrongByChoice.C: E. coli would typically grow on routine urine culture and is linked to urologic disease.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Mumps causes epididymitis usually with epididymo-orchitis after parotitis.

questions.stem: A 45-year-old competitive powerlifter develops right scrotal pain the day after an unusually heavy training session with prolonged straining. He sustained no direct blow to the groin. He is afebrile, monogamous and has no urinary symptoms. Urinalysis is normal and NAAT is negative. The right epididymis is tender. Which of the following is the most likely mechanism?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Ascending gonococcal urethral infection

choices.label: B
choices.text: Coliform infection from urinary stasis

choices.label: C
choices.text: Hematogenous spread of mumps virus

choices.label: D
choices.text: Loss of testicular blood flow from twisting

choices.label: E
choices.text: Reflux of urine along the genital ducts

explanation.summary: Urinary reflux into the epididymis from vigorous straining is a noninfectious cause of epididymitis.
explanation.whyCorrect: Noninfectious causes of epididymitis include trauma, autoimmune disease and urinary reflux into the epididymis due to vigorous straining. With no direct trauma, normal urinalysis and negative NAAT, reflux during heavy lifting best explains his findings.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Gonococcal epididymitis follows urethritis and NAAT would be positive.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Coliform infection with urinary stasis would usually produce pyuria.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Mumps orchitis typically follows parotitis in unvaccinated males.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Torsion causes sudden severe testicular pain with reduced blood flow, not isolated epididymal tenderness after straining.

questions.stem: A 40-year-old man had an episode of epididymitis 12 years ago that he never had treated. Since then he has had intermittent flares of mild epididymal pain. He and his partner now report 2 years of infertility. Which of the following most likely explains his infertility?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Hydroceles compressing both testes

choices.label: B
choices.text: Hypertrophy of the prostate blocking sperm flow

choices.label: C
choices.text: Scarring of the epididymis from chronic inflammation

choices.label: D
choices.text: Testicular ischemia from repeated torsion episodes

choices.label: E
choices.text: Viral destruction of the seminiferous tubules

explanation.summary: Untreated epididymitis can become chronic, and epididymal scarring can cause infertility.
explanation.whyCorrect: Complications of untreated acute epididymitis include epididymo-orchitis, chronic epididymitis, abscess and infertility. Chronic epididymitis is prolonged inflammation that can flare intermittently over a lifetime, and scarring of the epididymis can lead to infertility.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Hydroceles are not the recognized sequel of untreated epididymitis described here.
whyWrongByChoice.B: BPH predisposes older men to epididymitis but is not the explanation for infertility here.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Nothing in his history suggests torsion; his course fits chronic epididymitis.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Viral tubular destruction describes mumps orchitis, not untreated bacterial epididymitis.

questions.stem: A 58-year-old man has 3 days of right scrotal pain and swelling. Temperature is 39.2 C. Urinalysis and urine culture are sent. Which additional testing is indicated specifically because of his fever?

choices.label: A
choices.text: CBC and blood cultures

choices.label: B
choices.text: Mumps serology

choices.label: C
choices.text: RT-PCR of a saliva specimen

choices.label: D
choices.text: Serum anti-sperm antibodies

choices.label: E
choices.text: Testicular biopsy

explanation.summary: CBC and blood cultures are indicated when a patient with suspected orchitis or epididymitis is febrile.
explanation.whyCorrect: Urinalysis and culture are performed routinely regardless of suspected cause. CBC and blood cultures are indicated if the patient has a fever.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Mumps serology is used late in suspected mumps and is not triggered by fever.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Saliva RT-PCR diagnoses mumps, which is not suggested by fever alone in a 58-year-old.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Anti-sperm antibodies relate to autoimmune orchitis and are not indicated by fever.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Testicular biopsy is used to retrieve sperm in infertility, not in acute febrile workup.

questions.stem: A 45-year-old man with clinical findings of acute epididymitis has pyuria on urinalysis, but his urine culture shows no growth. Which of the following is the most accurate interpretation of the negative culture?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Cultures are unnecessary in men over 35

choices.label: B
choices.text: It establishes a viral etiology

choices.label: C
choices.text: It points toward testicular torsion instead

choices.label: D
choices.text: It reliably excludes a bacterial infection

choices.label: E
choices.text: Only about a quarter of cases grow bacteria

explanation.summary: Urine cultures are positive in only about a quarter of patients with epididymitis.
explanation.whyCorrect: Urinalysis and culture are routinely performed, and bacteria-related cases often show white cells, leukocyte esterase and pyuria. However, urine cultures are positive in only about a quarter of patients with epididymitis, so a negative culture does not rule out bacterial disease.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Urinalysis and culture are performed routinely regardless of age or suspected cause.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Pyuria argues for a bacterial process; viral orchitis typically has a normal urinalysis.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Culture results do not diagnose torsion; torsion is assessed clinically and by Doppler flow.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Most epididymitis cases have negative urine cultures, so a negative result does not exclude bacteria.

questions.stem: A 33-year-old man has epididymitis thought to result from an ascending bacterial infection. Which of the following urinalysis findings is most expected?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Entirely normal findings

choices.label: B
choices.text: Eosinophiluria with waxy casts

choices.label: C
choices.text: Glucosuria with ketonuria

choices.label: D
choices.text: Heme-positive dipstick without red cells

choices.label: E
choices.text: Leukocyte esterase with pyuria

explanation.summary: Bacteria-related epididymitis often shows increased white cells, positive leukocyte esterase and pyuria.
explanation.whyCorrect: Urinalysis in bacteria-related cases often shows increased white blood cells, positive leukocyte esterase and pyuria, reflecting infection ascending from the urethra, bladder or prostate.

whyWrongByChoice.A: A normal urinalysis is typical of isolated mumps orchitis, which spreads hematogenously.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Eosinophiluria with casts is not associated with bacterial epididymitis.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Glucosuria and ketonuria are not features of epididymitis.
whyWrongByChoice.D: A heme-positive dipstick without red cells is not the expected pattern here.

questions.stem: A 27-year-old man has gradual-onset left scrotal pain with urethral discharge. Scrotal ultrasonography is performed. Which of the following findings is most consistent with his likely diagnosis?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Absent testicular flow with a normal epididymis

choices.label: B
choices.text: Echogenic testicular mass with calcifications

choices.label: C
choices.text: Shrunken testis with uniformly reduced flow

choices.label: D
choices.text: Thick hypoechoic epididymis ringed by fluid

choices.label: E
choices.text: Thin hyperechoic epididymis without any fluid

explanation.summary: Epididymitis appears as a thickened, hypoechoic epididymis surrounded by fluid, often with increased flow.
explanation.whyCorrect: Ultrasound typically reveals epididymitis as a thickened, hypoechoic epididymis surrounded by fluid. The affected testis may show increased blood flow, and occasionally hypervascularity is the only finding.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Absent testicular flow suggests torsion, not epididymitis.
whyWrongByChoice.B: A testicular mass is not the ultrasound picture of epididymitis.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Reduced flow is the pattern of torsion; inflammation increases flow.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Epididymitis produces a thickened, hypoechoic epididymis, not a thin hyperechoic one.

questions.stem: An 18-year-old unvaccinated man has confirmed mumps and a swollen, tender left testis. Color Doppler ultrasonography of the left testis is most likely to show which of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Absent intratesticular blood flow

choices.label: B
choices.text: Hyperechoic testis with reduced flow

choices.label: C
choices.text: Increased flow and a hypoechoic testis

choices.label: D
choices.text: Isolated abscess with a normal testis

choices.label: E
choices.text: Normal flow and normal echotexture

explanation.summary: Mumps orchitis shows hyperemia and/or a hypoechoic testis on color Doppler.
explanation.whyCorrect: Color Doppler of mumps-related orchitis may show increased blood flow (hyperemia) and/or a hypoechoic, enlarged testis. This contrasts with the reduced flow of testicular torsion.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Absent flow indicates torsion, the time-sensitive surgical emergency.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Orchitis produces a hypoechoic testis with increased, not reduced, flow.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Abscess is a complication of destructive bacterial (coliform) epididymitis, not typical mumps orchitis.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Inflamed testes typically show hyperemia and altered echotexture.

questions.stem: A 25-year-old man with STI-associated epididymitis receives a single IM dose of ceftriaxone, but the oral agent that should accompany it is omitted. Which of the following likely pathogens remains inadequately covered?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Chlamydia trachomatis

choices.label: B
choices.text: Coxsackie B virus

choices.label: C
choices.text: Mumps orthorubulavirus

choices.label: D
choices.text: Neisseria gonorrhoeae

choices.label: E
choices.text: Treponema pallidum

explanation.summary: In the ceftriaxone-plus-doxycycline regimen, ceftriaxone covers N. gonorrhoeae and doxycycline covers C. trachomatis.
explanation.whyCorrect: Treatment for epididymitis in younger men targets both chlamydia and gonorrhea. Ceftriaxone covers N. gonorrhoeae, while doxycycline covers C. trachomatis, so omitting doxycycline leaves chlamydia untreated.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Coxsackie B is a rare viral cause of orchitis, not a target of this regimen.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Mumps is viral and is managed supportively, not by the omitted antibiotic.
whyWrongByChoice.D: N. gonorrhoeae is the organism ceftriaxone is given to cover.
whyWrongByChoice.E: T. pallidum is not the organism the omitted oral agent is intended to cover in this regimen.

questions.stem: A 29-year-old man with clinically diagnosed acute epididymitis has taken IM ceftriaxone and oral doxycycline as directed. On day 4 of therapy his pain and swelling are unchanged. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in reasoning?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Add levofloxacin to cover gram-positive cocci

choices.label: B
choices.text: Continue unchanged; improvement usually takes 3-4 weeks

choices.label: C
choices.text: Reconsider the diagnosis and evaluate other causes

choices.label: D
choices.text: Stop antibiotics, since most urine cultures are negative

choices.label: E
choices.text: Switch to supportive care for presumed mumps

explanation.summary: Acute epididymitis usually improves within 2-3 days of antibiotics; failure to improve should prompt consideration of other causes.
explanation.whyCorrect: Patients with acute epididymitis typically improve within 2-3 days of starting antibiotics. If symptoms do not improve, other causes of pain should be considered.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Adding drugs empirically ignores the need to consider other causes of the pain.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Improvement is expected within 2-3 days, not weeks.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Negative cultures are common in epididymitis and do not justify stopping therapy or explain lack of response.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Nothing suggests mumps; the lack of response should prompt a broader reassessment.

questions.stem: A 24-year-old man completed appropriate therapy for gonococcal epididymitis 2 months ago with full resolution. He now has recurrent urethral discharge and posterior testicular pain. He has continued having sex with the same partner, who has never been evaluated. Which of the following is the most likely explanation?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A structural genitourinary defect

choices.label: B
choices.text: Autoimmune breach of the blood-testis barrier

choices.label: C
choices.text: Hematogenous reactivation of mumps

choices.label: D
choices.text: Re-infection transmitted during intercourse

choices.label: E
choices.text: Urinary reflux from vigorous straining

explanation.summary: In sexually active men, recurrent epididymitis suggests re-infection from an infected partner.
explanation.whyCorrect: Epididymitis is sometimes recurrent. In sexually active men, recurrence suggests re-infection from an infected sexual partner, which is why partners must be treated and intercourse avoided until they are.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Structural defects are considered for recurrence in men who are not sexually active.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Autoimmune orchitis is a rare noninfectious condition and would not cause urethral discharge.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Mumps does not reactivate to cause urethral discharge.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Straining-related reflux is a noninfectious cause and does not explain recurrent discharge after partner exposure.

questions.stem: A 52-year-old man who has not been sexually active for several years has a third episode of E. coli epididymitis in 18 months. Each episode was treated with a full, adherently taken course of an antibiotic to which the isolate was susceptible, with prompt resolution. He has no urinary catheter. Which of the following should be suspected as the cause of his recurrences?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Coxsackie B viral syndrome

choices.label: B
choices.text: Intermittent testicular torsion

choices.label: C
choices.text: Re-infection from a sexual partner

choices.label: D
choices.text: Structural genitourinary defect

choices.label: E
choices.text: Undiagnosed mumps orchitis

explanation.summary: In men who are not sexually active, recurrent epididymitis suggests relapse from resistant organisms, inadequate treatment or a structural genitourinary defect.
explanation.whyCorrect: In men who are not sexually active, recurrence suggests relapse due to antibiotic-resistant organisms, inadequate initial treatment or structural genitourinary defects. With susceptible isolates and full adherent courses, a structural defect is the remaining explanation.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Coxsackie B is a rare viral cause of orchitis, unrelated to recurrent coliform epididymitis.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Torsion is a vascular emergency and does not cause culture-proven E. coli infection.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Re-infection from a partner explains recurrence in sexually active men; he has not been sexually active.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Mumps orchitis is viral and would not produce recurrent E. coli infection.

questions.stem: A 24-year-old man comes to the clinic because of 3 days of burning on urination and a thick yellow-green discharge from the tip of his penis. Examination shows several small pustules on the penile shaft. A swab of the discharge is Gram stained. Which of the following findings is most likely?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Abundant neutrophils with no visible organisms

choices.label: B
choices.text: Gram-negative diplococci within neutrophils

choices.label: C
