choices.text: Gram-negative rods scattered outside host cells

choices.label: D
choices.text: Gram-positive cocci in clusters within neutrophils

choices.label: E
choices.text: Gram-positive lancet-shaped diplococci outside cells

explanation.summary: Gonococcal urethritis produces purulent discharge whose Gram stain shows gram-negative diplococci inside phagocytes.
explanation.whyCorrect: Green, yellow, or white purulent urethral discharge with genital pustules and dysuria is the classic presentation of gonococcal urethritis. N. gonorrhoeae is a gram-negative, oxidase-positive diplococcus, and a Gram stain of a urethral swab shows the diplococci inside phagocytes, primarily neutrophils (occasionally some lie outside cells).

whyWrongByChoice.A: Neutrophils without visible organisms fit an organism that cannot be seen on Gram stain (e.g., C. trachomatis or M. genitalium), whose discharge is usually clear, not purulent.
whyWrongByChoice.C: N. gonorrhoeae is a diplococcus, not a rod, and it is classically seen inside neutrophils.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Gram-positive cocci in clusters describe staphylococci, not the cause of purulent urethritis with genital pustules.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Gram-positive lancet-shaped diplococci are not the pathogen of gonococcal urethritis, which stains gram-negative.

questions.stem: A 22-year-old woman has a cervical nucleic acid amplification test that is positive for Neisseria gonorrhoeae. Testing for other sexually transmitted infections was not performed. She is not pregnant and has no drug allergies. Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Intramuscular ceftriaxone once plus a single dose of azithromycin

choices.label: B
choices.text: Intramuscular ceftriaxone once plus doxycycline for 7 days

choices.label: C
choices.text: Intramuscular gentamicin once plus a single dose of azithromycin

choices.label: D
choices.text: Oral cefixime alone as a single dose

choices.label: E
choices.text: Oral doxycycline alone for 7 days

explanation.summary: Uncomplicated gonorrhea is treated with a single IM dose of ceftriaxone, plus 7 days of doxycycline when chlamydia has not been excluded.
explanation.whyCorrect: Ceftriaxone given once intramuscularly is the recommended treatment for uncomplicated gonorrhea. Because coinfection with C. trachomatis is common and chlamydia has not been excluded here, doxycycline for 7 days is added. This approach reflects rising gonococcal resistance and avoids routine azithromycin in nonpregnant adults.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Azithromycin is no longer preferred for empiric dual therapy in nonpregnant adults; doxycycline is the chlamydial add-on.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Gentamicin plus azithromycin is reserved for patients with a severe cephalosporin allergy, which she does not have.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Cefixime is an alternative only when ceftriaxone is unavailable, and alone it provides no chlamydial coverage.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Doxycycline alone covers chlamydia but does not treat the confirmed gonococcal infection.

questions.stem: A 19-year-old man requests screening for sexually transmitted infections after a new partner. He has no symptoms. He would prefer to avoid a urethral swab. Which of the following is the best test to detect both gonorrhea and chlamydia?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Cell culture of a urethral specimen for inclusions

choices.label: B
choices.text: Culture of a urethral specimen on selective agar

choices.label: C
choices.text: Gram stain of discharge expressed from the urethra

choices.label: D
choices.text: Nucleic acid amplification testing of a urine sample

choices.label: E
choices.text: Serum antibody titers against both organisms

explanation.summary: NAAT is the standard diagnostic test for both gonorrhea and chlamydia and can be run on urine.
explanation.whyCorrect: Nucleic acid amplification testing has largely replaced culture for routine diagnosis. It is highly sensitive and specific, faster, and less invasive because it can be performed on urine rather than a swab, and it allows concurrent testing for other STIs such as trichomonas.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Because C. trachomatis is obligately intracellular, culture is rarely performed clinically and it requires an invasive specimen.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Culture on selective (Thayer-Martin) media is used mainly for gonococcal surveillance and susceptibility testing and does not grow chlamydia.
whyWrongByChoice.C: A Gram stain can suggest gonorrhea but cannot identify C. trachomatis, which is obligately intracellular.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Serology is not how either infection is diagnosed; molecular testing is the standard.

questions.stem: A microbiologist studying Chlamydia trachomatis isolates the small, dense form of the organism that is released when an infected epithelial cell ruptures. Which of the following best describes this form?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It divides by binary fission inside the host inclusion

choices.label: B
choices.text: It generates its own ATP to survive outside cells

choices.label: C
choices.text: It has a thick wall of classic peptidoglycan

choices.label: D
choices.text: It is the infectious form that enters new host cells

choices.label: E
choices.text: It persists in soil and animal hosts between infections

explanation.summary: The chlamydial elementary body is the small, dense, infectious form that enters host cells.
explanation.whyCorrect: Chlamydiae exist in two forms. The elementary body is small, dense, and infectious; it enters host cells and converts to a reticulate body, which replicates by fission inside a membrane-bound inclusion before reorganizing into elementary bodies that are released to infect neighboring cells.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Replication by binary fission inside the inclusion is the job of the reticulate body, not the released elementary body.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Chlamydiae cannot make their own ATP, which is part of why they are obligate intracellular pathogens.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Chlamydiae lack classic peptidoglycan because of reduced muramic acid.
whyWrongByChoice.E: C. trachomatis is an obligate human pathogen with no animal or environmental reservoir.

questions.stem: Several candidate vaccines against Neisseria gonorrhoeae have generated strong antibody responses in trial participants yet failed to prevent infection. Which of the following properties of the organism best explains this failure?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A thick antiphagocytic polysaccharide capsule

choices.label: B
choices.text: Absence of a peptidoglycan cell wall

choices.label: C
choices.text: Antigenic and phase variation of pili and LOS

choices.label: D
choices.text: Obligate intracellular growth within inclusions

choices.label: E
choices.text: Secretion of a protease that cleaves IgG

explanation.summary: Antigenic and phase variation of gonococcal surface molecules lets the organism evade antibodies, undermining vaccines and permitting reinfection.
explanation.whyCorrect: Antibodies to pili, LOS, and other surface molecules can block binding, but these molecules undergo antigenic variation (structural change) and phase variation (reversible on/off switching of expression). The many variants escape neutralizing antibodies, which explains the poor efficacy of candidate vaccines and repeated infections.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Gonococci do not produce a capsule, unlike N. meningitidis.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Lack of a peptidoglycan cell wall describes M. genitalium; gonococci are gram-negative with a cell wall.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Obligate intracellular growth in inclusions describes C. trachomatis, not N. gonorrhoeae.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The gonococcal protease cleaves IgA, not IgG, and it is not the reason vaccines fail.

questions.stem: A 23-year-old woman being treated for cervical gonorrhea with pelvic inflammatory disease develops sharp right upper quadrant pain that worsens with deep breaths and coughing. She also has nausea and a temperature of 38.6°C (101.5°F). Inflammation of which of the following structures most likely explains her new pain?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The collecting system of the right kidney

choices.label: B
choices.text: The epithelium of the common bile duct

choices.label: C
choices.text: The Glisson capsule of the liver

choices.label: D
choices.text: The pleura of the right lower lobe

choices.label: E
choices.text: The wall of the gallbladder

explanation.summary: Fitz-Hugh-Curtis syndrome is perihepatitis (Glisson capsule inflammation) complicating PID.
explanation.whyCorrect: Fitz-Hugh-Curtis syndrome is a complication of PID in which the Glisson capsule surrounding the liver becomes inflamed. It classically causes right upper quadrant pain worsened by breathing, coughing, or movement, with nausea, vomiting, and fever.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Renal inflammation is not linked to ascending gonococcal PID in this way.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Bile duct infection is not the upper-abdominal complication associated with PID.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Although the pain is pleuritic in quality, the process is perihepatic, not pleural.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Gallbladder inflammation is not the recognized complication of gonococcal PID; the capsule around the liver is.

questions.stem: A 21-year-old sexually active woman comes to the emergency department with fever and pain moving between several joints over 4 days. Examination shows tenderness and swelling along the tendon sheaths of the right wrist and a few scattered skin lesions on her forearms and legs. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Disseminated gonococcal infection

choices.label: B
choices.text: Fitz-Hugh-Curtis syndrome

choices.label: C
choices.text: Lymphogranuloma venereum

choices.label: D
choices.text: Reactive arthritis

choices.label: E
choices.text: Staphylococcal septic arthritis

explanation.summary: Disseminated gonococcal infection classically presents with the triad of polyarthritis, tenosynovitis, and dermatitis.
explanation.whyCorrect: Disseminated gonococcal infection presents with polyarthritis, tenosynovitis, and dermatitis. This young, sexually active woman has all three: pain in several joints, tendon sheath inflammation at the wrist, and skin lesions on the extremities.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Fitz-Hugh-Curtis syndrome causes pleuritic right upper quadrant pain, not arthritis and skin lesions.
whyWrongByChoice.C: LGV presents with proctocolitis, anal ulcers, and painful inguinal lymphadenopathy, not joint and skin findings.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Reactive arthritis after chlamydia is a sterile arthritis of the knees, ankles, or feet and does not produce the tenosynovitis-dermatitis triad.
whyWrongByChoice.E: S. aureus septic arthritis typically involves a single joint and lacks tenosynovitis with dermatitis.

questions.stem: A 6-week-old boy is brought to the physician because of a repetitive cough that comes in short, separate bursts, along with rapid breathing. His mother received no prenatal care, and he was delivered vaginally at home. Chest x-ray shows bilateral interstitial infiltrates, and a complete blood count shows eosinophilia. Which of the following organisms is the most likely cause?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Chlamydia trachomatis

choices.label: B
choices.text: Mycoplasma genitalium

choices.label: C
choices.text: Neisseria gonorrhoeae

choices.label: D
choices.text: Neisseria meningitidis

choices.label: E
choices.text: Staphylococcus aureus

explanation.summary: Neonatal C. trachomatis pneumonia causes staccato cough, tachypnea, bilateral interstitial infiltrates, and eosinophilia.
explanation.whyCorrect: Infants born vaginally to a parent with chlamydia can develop conjunctivitis or pneumonia. Chlamydial neonatal pneumonia is characterized by a staccato cough, tachypnea, bilateral interstitial infiltrates, and eosinophilia, exactly as in this infant.

whyWrongByChoice.B: M. genitalium is discussed as a cause of persistent urethritis, not neonatal pneumonia.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Neonatal gonococcal infection presents as purulent ophthalmia neonatorum; neonatal pneumonia is a chlamydial manifestation.
whyWrongByChoice.D: N. meningitidis is not associated with this vertically acquired pneumonia syndrome.
whyWrongByChoice.E: S. aureus does not produce this staccato-cough, interstitial, eosinophilic picture.

questions.stem: A 27-year-old woman at 14 weeks' gestation undergoes routine prenatal screening. Nucleic acid amplification testing is positive for Chlamydia trachomatis and negative for Neisseria gonorrhoeae. She has no drug allergies. Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Intramuscular ceftriaxone

choices.label: B
choices.text: Intramuscular gentamicin

choices.label: C
choices.text: Oral azithromycin

choices.label: D
choices.text: Oral cefixime

choices.label: E
choices.text: Oral doxycycline

explanation.summary: When chlamydial coverage is needed in pregnancy, azithromycin is used because doxycycline is generally avoided.
explanation.whyCorrect: In nonpregnant adults doxycycline is the chlamydial agent, but it is generally avoided during pregnancy. The lecture specifies azithromycin for chlamydial coverage in pregnant patients.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Ceftriaxone is the gonococcal agent; her gonorrhea test is negative, and ceftriaxone does not treat chlamydia.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Gentamicin (with azithromycin) is an alternative gonorrhea regimen for severe cephalosporin allergy, not chlamydia therapy.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Cefixime is an alternative gonococcal agent when ceftriaxone is unavailable; it does not cover chlamydia.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Doxycycline is generally avoided in pregnancy and is used only if alternatives are unavailable.

questions.stem: A 4-day-old girl born in a hospital is brought to the clinic because of thick, purulent discharge from both eyes and marked eyelid swelling. Her parents declined all routine newborn medications after delivery. Gram stain of the discharge shows gram-negative diplococci within neutrophils. Which of the following is the most appropriate management?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Ceftriaxone, discharge home, and no evaluation of the mother

choices.label: B
choices.text: Ceftriaxone, evaluation for dissemination, and treating the mother

choices.label: C
choices.text: Erythromycin ointment, eye irrigation, and follow-up in one week

choices.label: D
choices.text: Oral azithromycin, chest radiograph, and reassurance of the mother

choices.label: E
choices.text: Topical erythromycin, lumbar puncture, and doxycycline for the mother

explanation.summary: Established gonococcal ophthalmia neonatorum requires ceftriaxone, evaluation for disseminated infection, and evaluation and treatment of the birthing parent.
explanation.whyCorrect: Purulent conjunctivitis 2-5 days after birth with gram-negative diplococci is gonococcal ophthalmia neonatorum. Once disease develops, erythromycin (a prophylactic agent) is no longer sufficient; standard treatment is ceftriaxone. The infant should be evaluated for disseminated infection, and the birthing parent should be evaluated and treated for gonorrhea.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Ceftriaxone is correct, but the infant must be assessed for dissemination and the birthing parent must be evaluated and treated.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Erythromycin ointment is prophylaxis given at birth; it is not sufficient treatment for established disease.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Azithromycin and a chest film fit a chlamydial picture; this is gonococcal disease, and the mother needs treatment, not reassurance.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Topical erythromycin is inadequate for established gonococcal disease, and doxycycline alone would not treat the mother's gonorrhea.

questions.stem: A 34-year-old man who has receptive anal intercourse comes to the physician because of 2 weeks of anal pain, fever, and a bloody, mucoid rectal discharge with a constant urge to defecate. Anoscopy shows several ulcers. One week later he develops painful, swollen inguinal lymph nodes. Which of the following is the most likely cause?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Chlamydia trachomatis serovars A, B, or C

choices.label: B
choices.text: Chlamydia trachomatis serovars D through K

choices.label: C
choices.text: Chlamydia trachomatis serovars L1, L2, or L3

choices.label: D
choices.text: Mycoplasma genitalium lacking a cell wall

choices.label: E
choices.text: Neisseria gonorrhoeae expressing variant pili

explanation.summary: Lymphogranuloma venereum (C. trachomatis L1-L3) presents in the US mainly as ulcerative proctocolitis that can progress to painful inguinal lymphadenopathy.
explanation.whyCorrect: LGV is a chronic infection caused by the more virulent, invasive C. trachomatis serovars L1, L2, and L3. Recent US cases have mostly presented as proctocolitis with anal ulcers, anal pain, mucoid or hemorrhagic rectal discharge, tenesmus, and fever, which may progress to painful inguinal lymphadenopathy.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Serovars A-C cause trachoma, an ocular infection spread by secretions, fomites, and flies.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Serovars D-K cause proctitis clinically similar to gonococcal proctitis, but ulcers with painful inguinal nodes point to the invasive L serovars.
whyWrongByChoice.D: M. genitalium is a cause of persistent urethritis, not ulcerative proctocolitis with lymphadenopathy.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Gonococcal proctitis causes itching, discharge, and tenesmus, but not ulcerative disease progressing to painful inguinal lymphadenopathy.

questions.stem: A 29-year-old woman is evaluated for infertility. Hysterosalpingography shows bilateral tubal scarring. She recalls a positive chlamydia screening test several years ago that was never treated, and she has never had pelvic pain or fever. Which of the following most directly caused the damage to her reproductive tract?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Cleavage of mucosal IgA by a bacterial protease

choices.label: B
choices.text: Direct lysis of epithelium by a secreted exotoxin

choices.label: C
choices.text: Endotoxin activity of bacterial lipooligosaccharide

choices.label: D
choices.text: Pilus-mediated resistance to neutrophil killing

choices.label: E
choices.text: Th1-driven chronic inflammation with IFN-γ release

explanation.summary: Chlamydial tissue damage is driven mainly by the host's Th1/IFN-γ immune response to persistent, often silent infection.
explanation.whyCorrect: Chlamydia-induced disease is driven largely by the host immune response. Persistent infection triggers chronic inflammation driven by Th1 cells and IFN-γ, and because infection is often asymptomatic, this immune-mediated damage can occur before diagnosis. Chlamydia causes PID more frequently and more silently than gonorrhea, hence its strong association with infertility and ectopic pregnancy.

whyWrongByChoice.A: IgA protease is a gonococcal virulence factor, not the mechanism of chlamydial scarring.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Injury from C. trachomatis is attributed to the immune response, not to a secreted exotoxin.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Lipooligosaccharide with endotoxin activity is a gonococcal virulence factor.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Pili that resist neutrophil killing belong to N. gonorrhoeae.

questions.stem: A county health officer reviews reported sexually transmitted infection data for the United States. Which of the following organisms causes the most commonly reported sexually transmitted infection?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Chlamydia trachomatis

choices.label: B
choices.text: Haemophilus ducreyi

choices.label: C
choices.text: Mycoplasma genitalium

choices.label: D
choices.text: Neisseria gonorrhoeae

choices.label: E
choices.text: Treponema pallidum

explanation.summary: Chlamydia is the most common STI in the US; gonorrhea is the second most common bacterial STI.
explanation.whyCorrect: Chlamydia is the most common sexually transmitted infection in the United States, most common in people aged 15-25. Routine screening of females adds to the number of reported cases.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Chancroid is not the most commonly reported STI; chlamydia is.
whyWrongByChoice.C: M. genitalium is discussed as a cause of persistent urethritis, not as the most common STI.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Gonorrhea is the second most common bacterial STI in the US, behind chlamydia.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Syphilis is not the most commonly reported STI; chlamydia is.

questions.stem: A 20-year-old man has had mild urethral irritation for 1 week. He notices a small amount of clear, watery discharge on his underwear in the mornings. He has no genital lesions or fever. Which of the following organisms is the most likely cause?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Chlamydia trachomatis

choices.label: B
choices.text: Neisseria gonorrhoeae

choices.label: C
choices.text: Neisseria meningitidis

choices.label: D
choices.text: Staphylococcus aureus

choices.label: E
choices.text: Streptococcus species

explanation.summary: Chlamydial urethritis is milder than gonococcal urethritis, with clear, watery or mucoid discharge.
explanation.whyCorrect: Chlamydia most commonly presents as urethritis with symptoms that are typically less severe than gonorrhea: a clear, watery, or mucoid urethral discharge with mild dysuria or urethral irritation. Non-gonococcal urethritis discharge is most often clear.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Gonococcal urethritis typically produces green, yellow, or white purulent discharge and can cause genital pustules.
whyWrongByChoice.C: N. meningitidis is not the usual cause of sexually acquired urethritis.
whyWrongByChoice.D: S. aureus is not a cause of this mild, clear urethral discharge.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Streptococci are listed as causes of septic arthritis, not of mild urethritis with clear discharge.

questions.stem: A healthy term boy is born by uncomplicated vaginal delivery in a hospital. Which of the following should be given shortly after birth to prevent gonococcal ophthalmia neonatorum?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Doxycycline eye drops

choices.label: B
choices.text: Erythromycin eye ointment

choices.label: C
choices.text: Intramuscular ceftriaxone

choices.label: D
choices.text: Intramuscular gentamicin

choices.label: E
choices.text: Oral azithromycin suspension

explanation.summary: All newborns should receive ocular erythromycin ointment shortly after birth.
explanation.whyCorrect: Routine prophylaxis with ocular erythromycin ointment shortly after birth prevents gonococcal ophthalmia neonatorum, which was common before universal newborn ocular prophylaxis was recommended.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Doxycycline is not the newborn prophylactic agent.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Ceftriaxone treats established gonococcal ophthalmia neonatorum; it is not routine prophylaxis for every newborn.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Gentamicin is an alternative adult gonorrhea regimen component for severe cephalosporin allergy, not newborn prophylaxis.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Oral azithromycin is not the recommended newborn ocular prophylaxis.

questions.stem: A 26-year-old woman with a history of pelvic inflammatory disease comes to the emergency department with lower abdominal pain and 7 weeks of amenorrhea. A pregnancy test is positive, and ultrasound shows an empty uterus with a mass beside the right ovary. Scarring of which of the following structures most directly predisposed her to this condition?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Endometrium

choices.label: B
choices.text: External cervical os

choices.label: C
choices.text: Glisson capsule

choices.label: D
choices.text: Ovarian capsule

choices.label: E
choices.text: Uterine tube

explanation.summary: PID scars the uterine tubes, leading to infertility and ectopic pregnancy.
explanation.whyCorrect: This is an ectopic pregnancy. Scarring of the uterine tubes from PID, caused by gonorrhea or (more silently) chlamydia, predisposes to both infertility and ectopic pregnancy.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The lecture ties the infertility and ectopic risk of PID to tubal scarring, not endometrial scarring.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The cervix is the route of ascent, but cervical scarring does not cause ectopic implantation.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Glisson capsule inflammation is Fitz-Hugh-Curtis perihepatitis and is unrelated to ectopic pregnancy.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Ovarian capsule scarring is not the recognized mechanism for ectopic pregnancy after PID.

questions.stem: A public health team is planning measures to interrupt transmission of gonorrhea and chlamydia in a community. Which of the following is the only known reservoir for both organisms?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Domestic poultry

choices.label: B
choices.text: Farm animals such as cattle

choices.label: C
choices.text: Infected humans

choices.label: D
choices.text: Rodents and their fleas

choices.label: E
choices.text: Soil and standing water

explanation.summary: N. gonorrhoeae and C. trachomatis are obligate human pathogens with no animal or environmental reservoir.
explanation.whyCorrect: Both pathogens are obligate human pathogens with no known animal or environmental reservoirs. Large numbers of asymptomatic infections provide the reservoir for ongoing transmission.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Neither organism has an avian reservoir.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Neither organism has a livestock reservoir.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Neither organism is maintained in rodents or transmitted by fleas.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Neither organism has an environmental reservoir.

questions.stem: A urethral isolate grows as gram-negative, oxidase-positive diplococci that metabolize glucose. The laboratory must decide whether it is Neisseria gonorrhoeae or Neisseria meningitidis. Which of the following findings would identify it as N. gonorrhoeae?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A positive oxidase reaction

choices.label: B
choices.text: Absence of maltose fermentation

choices.label: C
choices.text: Growth on Thayer-Martin selective media

choices.label: D
choices.text: Metabolism of glucose as a carbon source

choices.label: E
choices.text: Presence of a polysaccharide capsule

explanation.summary: Unlike N. meningitidis, N. gonorrhoeae does not ferment maltose and lacks a capsule.
explanation.whyCorrect: Both Neisseria species are gram-negative, oxidase-positive diplococci that metabolize glucose. Gonococci differ from meningococci in that they do not ferment maltose and do not produce a capsule.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Both species are oxidase-positive.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Thayer-Martin media is used to grow Neisseria species generally, so growth does not separate the two.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Both species metabolize glucose.
whyWrongByChoice.E: A capsule points to N. meningitidis; gonococci do not produce one.

questions.stem: A medical student asks why the laboratory can grow Neisseria gonorrhoeae on agar plates but cannot grow Chlamydia trachomatis the same way. Which of the following characteristics of C. trachomatis best explains the difference?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It depends on host cells for ATP

choices.label: B
choices.text: It ferments neither glucose nor maltose

choices.label: C
choices.text: It is killed by vancomycin in selective media

choices.label: D
choices.text: It produces a capsule that blocks nutrient uptake

choices.label: E
choices.text: It requires a passage through an animal host

explanation.summary: Chlamydiae cannot make their own ATP and are obligate intracellular pathogens, so they do not grow on cell-free media.
explanation.whyCorrect: All Chlamydiae are obligate intracellular pathogens: they cannot make their own ATP and must replicate inside host cells. For that reason, staining and culture of C. trachomatis are rarely performed clinically, and diagnosis relies on NAAT.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Sugar fermentation is used to distinguish Neisseria species, not to explain chlamydial growth requirements.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Vancomycin in Thayer-Martin media inhibits gram-positive organisms; it is not why chlamydia fails to grow on agar.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The lecture does not describe a chlamydial capsule; its limitation is energy dependence on the host.
whyWrongByChoice.E: C. trachomatis is an obligate human pathogen with no animal reservoir.

questions.stem: A state health department finds that gonorrhea case rates are highest in rural counties of the southeastern United States that have few clinics and long travel times to care. Which of the following factors most likely contributes to these higher rates?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A higher proportion of symptomatic infections

choices.label: B
choices.text: Environmental reservoirs of the organism in the region

choices.label: C
choices.text: Greater intrinsic susceptibility of local residents

choices.label: D
choices.text: Limited access to and use of health services

choices.label: E
choices.text: More frequent use of newborn eye prophylaxis

explanation.summary: Disparities in gonorrhea rates reflect differences in health services access and utilization, among other social factors.
explanation.whyCorrect: Differences in access to and use of health services, sexual network patterns along socioeconomic and racial lines, and differential reporting produce disparities in gonorrhea prevalence. Rates are higher where access to care is poor, such as parts of the southeastern US.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Most gonococcal infections are asymptomatic; poor access delays detection and treatment regardless of symptoms.
whyWrongByChoice.B: N. gonorrhoeae has no environmental reservoir; humans are the only reservoir.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Disparities are attributed to access, partner networks, and reporting, not intrinsic biological susceptibility.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Newborn eye prophylaxis prevents ophthalmia neonatorum and would not raise adult case rates.

questions.stem: A 34-year-old man comes to the physician because of 3 days of pain between the scrotum and anus and above the pubic bone. He also reports burning with urination, urinary urgency and frequency, and pain with ejaculation that radiates to the tip of the penis. The scrotum is not swollen. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Acute bacterial prostatitis

choices.label: B
choices.text: Acute epididymitis

choices.label: C
choices.text: Fitz-Hugh-Curtis syndrome

choices.label: D
choices.text: Lymphogranuloma venereum

choices.label: E
choices.text: Reactive arthritis

explanation.summary: Acute bacterial prostatitis causes perineal or suprapubic pain, dysuria, urgency or frequency, and painful ejaculation.
explanation.whyCorrect: Acute bacterial prostatitis commonly causes perineal or suprapubic pain, dysuria, and urinary frequency or urgency, and may be associated with painful ejaculation and pain radiating to the penis or testicles. Both gonorrhea and chlamydia can cause prostatitis.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Epididymitis presents with unilateral scrotal pain, epididymal tenderness, and swelling, which he lacks.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Fitz-Hugh-Curtis syndrome is perihepatitis complicating PID in females.
whyWrongByChoice.D: LGV presents with proctocolitis, anal ulcers, and painful inguinal lymphadenopathy.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Reactive arthritis is a sterile arthritis of the knees, ankles, or feet.

questions.stem: A previously healthy, sexually active 20-year-old woman has a 2-day history of fever and a hot, swollen, painful right knee. Arthrocentesis is performed, and Gram stain of the fluid shows gram-negative diplococci. Which of the following synovial fluid findings is most likely?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Bloody fluid, few leukocytes, many erythrocytes

choices.label: B
choices.text: Clear fluid, 200 cells/µL, mostly lymphocytes

choices.label: C
choices.text: Purulent fluid, >50,000 cells/µL, mostly eosinophils

choices.label: D
choices.text: Purulent fluid, >50,000 cells/µL, mostly neutrophils

choices.label: E
choices.text: Straw-colored fluid, 3,000 cells/µL, mixed cells

explanation.summary: Septic arthritis produces purulent synovial fluid with markedly elevated, neutrophil-predominant leukocytes (often >50,000/µL).
explanation.whyCorrect: Gonococcal arthritis is the most common cause of septic arthritis in young, otherwise healthy adults, especially females, and often involves a large weight-bearing joint such as the knee. Synovial fluid is purulent with markedly elevated leukocytes, often >50,000 cells/µL with neutrophil predominance. Untreated, it can destroy cartilage and spread to bone or cause sepsis.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Bloody fluid with few leukocytes does not reflect an infected joint.
whyWrongByChoice.B: A low, lymphocytic count does not fit an acute bacterial joint infection.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The count fits, but septic arthritis is neutrophil predominant, not eosinophil predominant.
whyWrongByChoice.E: A modest mixed cell count is far below the purulent, neutrophil-rich fluid of septic arthritis.

questions.stem: A 19-year-old man with multiple male sexual partners has a 5-day history of sore throat. Examination shows tonsillar exudates and tender anterior cervical lymph nodes. A rapid streptococcal test is negative, and a throat culture on Thayer-Martin media grows oxidase-positive, gram-negative diplococci. By which of the following routes did this organism most likely reach his pharynx?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Direct mucosal contact during oral sex

choices.label: B
choices.text: Fomites such as shared drinking cups

choices.label: C
choices.text: Hematogenous spread from a genital infection

choices.label: D
choices.text: Ingestion of contaminated food or water

choices.label: E
choices.text: Respiratory droplets from a household contact

explanation.summary: Gonococcal pharyngitis is acquired by direct oral sexual contact; mucosal infections reflect the nature of contact.
explanation.whyCorrect: N. gonorrhoeae infects many mucosal surfaces, and these infections are tied directly to the nature of contact; it is transmitted by vaginal, oral, or anal sex or to neonates during birth. Gonococcal pharyngitis can be asymptomatic or cause sore throat, pharyngeal exudates, and cervical lymphadenitis.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Gonorrhea is spread by sexual contact, not casual fomites; fomite spread is a feature of trachoma.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Hematogenous spread produces disseminated infection (arthritis, tenosynovitis, dermatitis), not isolated pharyngitis.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Gonorrhea is not a food- or waterborne infection.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Gonorrhea is not spread by respiratory droplets.

questions.stem: A 25-year-old woman at 20 weeks' gestation has fever, lower abdominal pain, and a purulent cervical discharge. Pelvic examination shows cervical motion tenderness, and she is diagnosed with pelvic inflammatory disease. Which of the following is the most appropriate management?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Hospital admission with parenteral antibiotics

choices.label: B
choices.text: Observation without antibiotics until NAAT returns

choices.label: C
choices.text: Outpatient IM ceftriaxone plus oral doxycycline

choices.label: D
choices.text: Outpatient oral azithromycin given alone

choices.label: E
choices.text: Outpatient oral cefixime with 1-week follow-up

explanation.summary: Pregnant patients with PID should be hospitalized and treated with parenteral antibiotics.
explanation.whyCorrect: Pregnant patients with PID should be hospitalized and given parenteral antibiotics to reduce the risk of maternal and fetal complications.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Withholding treatment risks maternal and fetal complications; she needs admission and parenteral therapy now.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Outpatient therapy is inappropriate for PID in pregnancy, and doxycycline is generally avoided during pregnancy.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Azithromycin alone is chlamydial coverage and is not adequate outpatient management of PID in pregnancy.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Cefixime is an alternative only for selected uncomplicated gonorrhea when ceftriaxone is unavailable, not for PID in pregnancy.

questions.stem: An 11-day-old girl is brought to the physician because of mild redness of both eyes and a small amount of slightly mucoid discharge for 2 days. She was delivered vaginally, and she is feeding well. Which of the following organisms is the most likely cause?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Chlamydia trachomatis

choices.label: B
choices.text: Mycoplasma genitalium

choices.label: C
choices.text: Neisseria gonorrhoeae

choices.label: D
choices.text: Neisseria meningitidis

choices.label: E
choices.text: Staphylococcus aureus

explanation.summary: Chlamydial neonatal conjunctivitis is less purulent and appears later (5-14 days) than gonococcal ophthalmia neonatorum (2-5 days).
explanation.whyCorrect: Chlamydial neonatal conjunctivitis is typically less purulent than gonococcal conjunctivitis and has a longer incubation, appearing about 5-14 days after birth. Onset near day 9 with mild, mucoid discharge fits chlamydia.

whyWrongByChoice.B: M. genitalium is a cause of persistent urethritis, not neonatal conjunctivitis.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Gonococcal ophthalmia neonatorum appears earlier (2-5 days after birth) with frankly purulent discharge and eyelid swelling.
whyWrongByChoice.D: N. meningitidis is not a cause of vertically acquired neonatal conjunctivitis.
whyWrongByChoice.E: S. aureus is not the vertically transmitted cause of this mild, later-onset neonatal conjunctivitis in the lecture.

questions.stem: Investigators create a mutant strain of Neisseria gonorrhoeae that cannot assemble its long, hair-like surface appendages. Compared with the wild-type strain, the mutant is most likely to show reduced ability to do which of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Attach to host epithelial cells

choices.label: B
choices.text: Cleave mucosal immunoglobulin A

choices.label: C
choices.text: Exert endotoxin activity

choices.label: D
choices.text: Metabolize glucose

choices.label: E
choices.text: Replicate within membrane-bound inclusions

explanation.summary: Gonococcal pili mediate attachment to host cells, bacterial aggregation, and resistance to neutrophil killing.
explanation.whyCorrect: Pili are long, hair-like appendages that mediate attachment to host cells, bacterial aggregation, and resistance to neutrophil killing. Without pili the organism would adhere poorly to host epithelium.

whyWrongByChoice.B: IgA cleavage is performed by IgA protease, a separate virulence factor.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Endotoxin activity comes from lipooligosaccharide (LOS), not pili.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Glucose metabolism is a biochemical property unrelated to pili.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Replication in membrane-bound inclusions describes C. trachomatis, not gonococci.

questions.stem: A 23-year-old woman with disseminated gonococcal infection is febrile and hypotensive. Which of the following gonococcal components, a variant of the outer-membrane molecule of other gram-negative bacteria, has strong endotoxin activity and masks the organism's protein antigens?

choices.label: A
choices.text: IgA protease

choices.label: B
choices.text: Lipooligosaccharide

choices.label: C
choices.text: Peptidoglycan

choices.label: D
choices.text: Pilin

choices.label: E
choices.text: Polysaccharide capsule

explanation.summary: Gonococcal lipooligosaccharide (LOS) is an LPS variant with strong endotoxin activity that also masks protein antigens.
explanation.whyCorrect: LOS is a form of LPS with strong endotoxin activity. It mediates binding to some host cells and masks proteinaceous antigens. Like pili, it undergoes antigenic and phase variation.

whyWrongByChoice.A: IgA protease cleaves IgA; it has no endotoxin activity.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Peptidoglycan is not the gonococcal endotoxin described in the lecture.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Pilin forms pili, which mediate attachment and resist neutrophil killing but are not endotoxins.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Gonococci do not produce a capsule.

questions.stem: Secretions from the cervix of a woman with gonorrhea contain fragments of the predominant antibody class found on mucosal surfaces. Which of the following gonococcal virulence factors is most likely responsible for these fragments?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Beta-lactamase

choices.label: B
choices.text: IgA protease

choices.label: C
choices.text: Lipooligosaccharide

choices.label: D
choices.text: Pili

choices.label: E
choices.text: Polysaccharide capsule

explanation.summary: Gonococcal IgA protease recognizes and cleaves IgA, the main mucosal antibody.
explanation.whyCorrect: IgA protease is a gonococcal virulence factor that recognizes and cleaves IgA, blunting antibody defense at mucosal surfaces.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Beta-lactamase is not among the virulence factors described and does not cleave antibody.
whyWrongByChoice.C: LOS has endotoxin activity and masks protein antigens but does not cleave antibody.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Pili mediate attachment, aggregation, and neutrophil resistance, not antibody cleavage.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Gonococci lack a capsule.

questions.stem: A 25-year-old man was treated for chlamydial urethritis 3 weeks ago. He now has a painful, swollen left knee and right ankle. Arthrocentesis fluid shows no organisms on Gram stain, and cultures remain sterile. Which of the following best explains his joint symptoms?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Endotoxin released by circulating lipooligosaccharide

choices.label: B
choices.text: Gonococcal infection of the adjacent tendon sheaths

choices.label: C
choices.text: Hematogenous seeding of live organisms into synovium

choices.label: D
choices.text: Immune-mediated inflammation without synovial infection

choices.label: E
choices.text: Pilus-mediated bacterial adherence to cartilage

explanation.summary: C. trachomatis can trigger reactive arthritis, a sterile, immune-mediated arthritis of the knees, ankles, or feet.
explanation.whyCorrect: Reactive arthritis is a sterile arthritis mediated by the immune response that can follow C. trachomatis infection. It most often affects the knees, ankles, or feet, matching his sterile joint fluid and distribution.

whyWrongByChoice.A: LOS is a gonococcal endotoxin and does not explain post-chlamydial sterile arthritis.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Gonococcal tenosynovitis is part of disseminated gonococcal infection, not a sterile post-chlamydial process.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Hematogenous seeding causes septic arthritis with purulent fluid and positive culture, not sterile fluid.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Pili are a gonococcal adherence factor, and this joint contains no organisms.

questions.stem: An 8-year-old child living in a village with poor sanitation has had repeated episodes of follicular conjunctivitis. Examination now shows conjunctival scarring, and the upper eyelid has turned inward so the eyelashes scrape the cornea. Which of the following is the most likely mode of transmission of the responsible organism?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Drinking water contaminated by animal waste

choices.label: B
choices.text: Inhalation of respiratory droplets from a sick sibling

choices.label: C
choices.text: Ocular secretions carried by hands, fomites, or flies

choices.label: D
choices.text: Passage through an infected birth canal

choices.label: E
choices.text: Sexual contact with an infected adult

explanation.summary: Trachoma (C. trachomatis serovars A-C) spreads through ocular secretions, contaminated fomites, and eye-seeking flies where sanitation is poor.
explanation.whyCorrect: Trachoma is a chronic ocular infection by C. trachomatis serovars A, B, or C, transmitted through direct contact with ocular secretions, contaminated fomites, or eye-seeking flies, particularly with poor sanitation. Repeated infection causes follicular conjunctivitis and scarring, then entropion with trichiasis, corneal opacity, and blindness; it is the leading infectious cause of blindness worldwide.

whyWrongByChoice.A: C. trachomatis has no animal or environmental reservoir, so water contaminated by animal waste is not a source.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Trachoma is not described as spreading by respiratory droplets.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Birth-canal acquisition causes neonatal conjunctivitis or pneumonia, not recurrent childhood trachoma.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Sexual transmission characterizes the genital serovars (D-K and L1-L3), not trachoma.

questions.stem: A 24-year-old man has uncomplicated gonococcal urethritis confirmed by NAAT; testing for chlamydia is negative. He reports developing hives after taking amoxicillin as a child and has never received a cephalosporin. Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Intramuscular ceftriaxone given as a single dose

choices.label: B
choices.text: Intramuscular gentamicin plus oral azithromycin

choices.label: C
choices.text: Oral azithromycin given as a single dose

choices.label: D
choices.text: Oral cefixime given as a single dose

choices.label: E
choices.text: Oral doxycycline given for 7 days

explanation.summary: Ceftriaxone is still generally used in penicillin-allergic patients because cross-reactivity with third-generation cephalosporins is low (<2.5%).
explanation.whyCorrect: Cross-reactivity between penicillin and third-generation cephalosporins is low (<2.5%), so a single IM dose of ceftriaxone remains the treatment of choice. Chlamydia has been excluded, so no doxycycline is needed.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Gentamicin plus azithromycin is reserved for a severe cephalosporin allergy, which he does not have.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Azithromycin alone does not reliably treat gonorrhea and is no longer preferred in empiric therapy for nonpregnant adults.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Cefixime is an alternative only when ceftriaxone is unavailable.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Doxycycline covers chlamydia, which has been excluded, and does not treat gonorrhea.

questions.stem: A laboratory prepares its own batch of the selective medium used to culture Neisseria from urethral specimens, but one additive is accidentally left out. Plates inoculated with urethral specimens become overgrown by gram-positive cocci. Which of the following additives was most likely omitted?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Colistin

choices.label: B
choices.text: Erythromycin

choices.label: C
choices.text: Nystatin

choices.label: D
choices.text: Trimethoprim

choices.label: E
choices.text: Vancomycin

explanation.summary: In Thayer-Martin media, vancomycin suppresses gram-positive organisms.
explanation.whyCorrect: Thayer-Martin is a selective medium containing vancomycin, trimethoprim, colistin, and nystatin. Vancomycin inhibits gram-positive organisms, so leaving it out allows gram-positive overgrowth.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Colistin inhibits gram-negative species of other genera, not gram-positive cocci.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Erythromycin is the newborn ocular prophylactic, not a Thayer-Martin component.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Nystatin prevents fungal growth.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Trimethoprim inhibits gram-negative species of other genera.

questions.stem: A study finds a high rate of asymptomatic Chlamydia trachomatis infection among sexually active 16- to 19-year-old females compared with women in their 30s. Which of the following cervical changes in the younger group best explains their greater susceptibility?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Absence of IgA from immature cervical secretions

choices.label: B
choices.text: Eversion of columnar endocervical epithelium onto the ectocervix

choices.label: C
choices.text: Loss of mucus-secreting glands in the endocervical canal

choices.label: D
choices.text: Replacement of cervical epithelium by keratinized squamous cells

choices.label: E
choices.text: Thickening of stratified squamous ectocervical epithelium

explanation.summary: Estrogen-driven cervical ectopy exposes columnar epithelium, the cell type C. trachomatis preferentially infects.
explanation.whyCorrect: Cervical ectopy, the eversion of endocervical columnar epithelium onto the ectocervix, occurs in high-estrogen states such as adolescence. Because C. trachomatis preferentially infects columnar epithelial cells, greater ectopy increases susceptibility and high rates of asymptomatic infection in females under 25.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The lecture attributes adolescent susceptibility to ectopy, not to absent IgA.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Loss of endocervical glands would not expand the columnar surface chlamydia infects.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Keratinized squamous replacement would reduce, not increase, the columnar target cells.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Thicker squamous epithelium would present fewer columnar target cells, not more.

questions.stem: After entering a urogenital columnar epithelial cell, Chlamydia trachomatis converts to its replicating form and remains enclosed within a membrane-bound vacuole for the rest of its developmental cycle. Which of the following is the principal advantage of this arrangement for the organism?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It allows release of lipooligosaccharide endotoxin

choices.label: B
choices.text: It allows synthesis of a classic peptidoglycan wall

choices.label: C
choices.text: It confers resistance to vancomycin and colistin

choices.label: D
choices.text: It enables phase variation of surface pilus proteins

choices.label: E
choices.text: It shields it from lysosomal destruction

explanation.summary: C. trachomatis replicates within a membrane-bound inclusion that avoids lysosomal destruction; intracellular location also shields it from antibody and complement.
explanation.whyCorrect: Elementary bodies convert to reticulate bodies that stay within a membrane-bound inclusion, where the organism avoids lysosomal destruction and replicates by binary fission. Intracellular localization also protects it from antibodies and complement.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Lipooligosaccharide endotoxin is a gonococcal virulence factor.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Chlamydiae lack classic peptidoglycan because of reduced muramic acid.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Vancomycin and colistin are Thayer-Martin additives for culturing Neisseria, unrelated to chlamydial inclusions.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Phase variation of pili is a gonococcal immune-evasion strategy.

questions.stem: A 28-year-old man was treated with intramuscular ceftriaxone and 7 days of doxycycline for urethritis 3 weeks ago, but his mucoid urethral discharge and dysuria persist. Gram stain of the discharge shows neutrophils but no organisms. The most likely causative organism is not visible on Gram stain for which of the following reasons?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It has a thick polysaccharide capsule

choices.label: B
choices.text: It hides inside neutrophils and resists staining

choices.label: C
choices.text: It lacks a peptidoglycan cell wall

choices.label: D
choices.text: It replicates only within host cell inclusions

choices.label: E
choices.text: It undergoes rapid phase variation of its pili

explanation.summary: Urethritis persisting after standard gonorrhea/chlamydia therapy suggests Mycoplasma genitalium, which lacks a peptidoglycan wall and needs NAAT for diagnosis.
explanation.whyCorrect: Urethritis that persists despite standard empiric treatment for chlamydia and gonorrhea may be caused by Mycoplasma genitalium, which closely mimics C. trachomatis. It cannot be seen on Gram stain because it lacks a peptidoglycan cell wall, so diagnosis requires NAAT, and treatment is difficult because of high macrolide resistance.

whyWrongByChoice.A: A capsule does not prevent Gram staining, and the lecture does not describe one for this organism.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Gonococci within neutrophils are readily visible on Gram stain as gram-negative diplococci.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Obligate replication within inclusions describes C. trachomatis, which should have been treated by the doxycycline course.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Phase variation of pili is a gonococcal immune-evasion trait and does not affect Gram stain visibility.

questions.stem: A 30-year-old woman has uncomplicated cervical gonorrhea; chlamydia NAAT is negative. She is not pregnant. Two years ago she had anaphylaxis within minutes of receiving intravenous cefazolin before surgery. Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Intramuscular ceftriaxone plus oral doxycycline

choices.label: B
choices.text: Intramuscular gentamicin plus oral azithromycin

choices.label: C
choices.text: Oral azithromycin as monotherapy

choices.label: D
choices.text: Oral cefixime plus oral doxycycline

choices.label: E
choices.text: Oral doxycycline as monotherapy

explanation.summary: For a severe cephalosporin allergy, an alternative gonorrhea regimen such as gentamicin plus azithromycin is used.
explanation.whyCorrect: Anaphylaxis to cefazolin is a severe cephalosporin allergy, so ceftriaxone and cefixime should be avoided. The lecture lists gentamicin plus azithromycin as an alternative regimen in this situation.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Ceftriaxone is a cephalosporin and is contraindicated after cephalosporin anaphylaxis.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Azithromycin monotherapy is not a recommended gonorrhea regimen.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Cefixime is also a cephalosporin; it is the alternative when ceftriaxone is unavailable, not when cephalosporins are contraindicated.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Doxycycline provides chlamydial coverage and does not treat gonorrhea.

questions.stem: A 27-year-old man presents with 5 days of fever, sore throat, fatigue, and painful oral ulcers. Examination shows generalized lymphadenopathy and a faint maculopapular rash on his face, trunk, and extremities. Four weeks ago he had condomless receptive anal intercourse with a new partner. His CD4+ T cell count is 780/uL. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Acute retroviral syndrome of HIV infection

choices.label: B
choices.text: Clinically latent chronic HIV infection

choices.label: C
choices.text: Kaposi sarcoma in the setting of AIDS

choices.label: D
choices.text: Primary genital herpes simplex infection

choices.label: E
choices.text: Seborrheic dermatitis in the setting of AIDS

explanation.summary: Acute retroviral syndrome is a mononucleosis-like illness 3-6 weeks after HIV exposure with fever, pharyngitis, lymphadenopathy, maculopapular rash, and mucocutaneous ulcers.
explanation.whyCorrect: Many patients (40-90%) develop acute retroviral syndrome during the acute phase (0-12 weeks), most often 3-6 weeks after infection. Features include fever, lethargy, sore throat, generalized lymphadenopathy, a diffuse maculopapular rash of the face, trunk, and extremities, and mucocutaneous ulcerations. CD4+ counts may dip transiently but can remain in the normal range (500-1500/uL), as here.

whyWrongByChoice.B: The chronic phase is clinically latent and asymptomatic; this patient is acutely symptomatic weeks after exposure.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Kaposi sarcoma is a secondary neoplasm of AIDS; a CD4 count of 780/uL and a new febrile rash weeks after exposure do not fit.
whyWrongByChoice.D: HSV causes mucocutaneous ulcers but not a diffuse maculopapular rash with generalized lymphadenopathy and systemic illness after a high-risk exposure.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Seborrheic dermatitis produces red, flaky, greasy lesions in advanced disease, not an acute febrile maculopapular illness with a normal CD4 count.

questions.stem: A fourth-generation HIV screening immunoassay detects a viral capsid antigen, p24, in addition to host IgM and IgG against HIV-1/2. Which HIV gene encodes this antigen?

choices.label: A
choices.text: env

choices.label: B
choices.text: gag

choices.label: C
choices.text: pol

choices.label: D
choices.text: rev

choices.label: E
choices.text: tat

explanation.summary: gag encodes the structural proteins p24, p7, and p17 of the nucleocapsid and matrix.
explanation.whyCorrect: Three HIV genes encode proteins critical to its life cycle. gag encodes the structural proteins p24, p7, and p17 used in the nucleocapsid and matrix. p24 is the antigen detected by the HIV-1/2 antigen/antibody immunoassay.

whyWrongByChoice.A: env encodes the envelope glycoproteins gp120 and gp41 that mediate fusion.
whyWrongByChoice.C: pol encodes the enzymes reverse transcriptase, integrase, and protease, not structural capsid proteins.
whyWrongByChoice.D: rev is not one of the three genes described as encoding HIV structural proteins; p24 comes from gag.
whyWrongByChoice.E: tat is not one of the three genes described as encoding HIV structural proteins; p24 comes from gag.

questions.stem: A 38-year-old man with HIV has had an undetectable plasma viral load on antiretroviral therapy for several years. Researchers studying tissue from patients like him identify infected cells that express CD4 with the CCR5 coreceptor and that resist infection-associated apoptosis and cytotoxic T cell killing. Which cell type is most likely serving as this viral reservoir?

choices.label: A
choices.text: CD4+ helper T lymphocytes

choices.label: B
choices.text: CD8+ cytotoxic T lymphocytes

choices.label: C
choices.text: Circulating neutrophils

choices.label: D
choices.text: Macrophages

choices.label: E
choices.text: Natural killer cells

explanation.summary: Macrophages and dendritic cells are less susceptible to infection-associated death and may serve as HIV reservoirs.
explanation.whyCorrect: HIV infects cells expressing CD4 plus at least one coreceptor (CCR5 or CXCR4): CD4+ T cells, macrophages, and dendritic cells. Infected CD4+ helper T cells are susceptible to apoptosis and immune-mediated killing, whereas macrophages and dendritic cells are less susceptible to infection-associated death and may act as reservoirs of the virus.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Infected CD4+ helper T cells are particularly susceptible to apoptosis and cytotoxic T cell killing, the opposite of the described resistance.
whyWrongByChoice.B: CD8+ cytotoxic T cells are effectors that kill infected cells; they are not described as HIV targets.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Neutrophils are not listed among the CD4-bearing cells HIV infects.
whyWrongByChoice.E: NK cells contribute to CD4+ T cell destruction through antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity; they are not the reservoir.

questions.stem: A 35-year-old woman was diagnosed with HIV 4 years ago and declined treatment. She has been asymptomatic since a brief febrile illness at the time of infection, and her CD4+ T cell count has been stable at 600-650/uL. Which of the following best describes HIV activity in her body at this time?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Active replication, mainly in lymphoid tissue, at a set-point

choices.label: B
choices.text: Exponentially rising viremia outpacing the immune response

choices.label: C
choices.text: Replication confined to CNS cells behind the blood-brain barrier

choices.label: D
choices.text: Virus cleared from tissues by neutralizing anti-HIV IgG

choices.label: E
choices.text: Virus dormant as provirus with no ongoing replication

explanation.summary: Clinical latency is not viral latency: in the chronic phase HIV actively replicates, mainly in lymphoid tissue, at a steady set-point viral load.
explanation.whyCorrect: During the chronic phase patients are clinically latent and asymptomatic, but the virus is not latent. HIV actively replicates in the host, primarily in lymphoid tissues, and the viral load typically settles at a baseline set-point that stays steady for years.

whyWrongByChoice.B: The virus outcompeting the immune response describes the crisis (AIDS) phase, not a stable CD4 count years into infection.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Replication in the chronic phase occurs primarily in lymphoid tissues, not only in the CNS.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Anti-HIV IgG neutralizes and opsonizes free virions but does not clear the infection.
whyWrongByChoice.E: This confuses clinical latency with viral latency; the virus keeps replicating during the chronic phase.

questions.stem: Two 30-year-old men acquired HIV at about the same time and are both asymptomatic and untreated, with similar CD4+ T cell counts. Their physician wants the laboratory value that measures the replicative rate of each man's infection and whose baseline level best predicts how quickly each will progress. Which measurement should be followed?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Absolute CD4+ T cell count

choices.label: B
choices.text: Absolute CD8+ T cell count

choices.label: C
choices.text: Anti-HIV IgM antibody titer

choices.label: D
choices.text: Qualitative p24 antigen result

choices.label: E
choices.text: Set-point plasma viral load

explanation.summary: Viral load measures replicative rate, and a higher baseline (set-point) viral load predicts faster progression.
explanation.whyCorrect: Viral load should be monitored because it measures the replicative rate of the infection and its potential to destroy the cellular immune system. The baseline (set-point) viral load is a strong predictor of disease progression: a higher baseline correlates with faster progression.

whyWrongByChoice.A: CD4+ count gauges the current extent of immune compromise, opportunistic-infection risk, and prophylaxis needs; it does not measure viral replication.
whyWrongByChoice.B: CD8+ counts are not used to measure viral replication or predict progression.
whyWrongByChoice.C: IgM against HIV is part of the screening immunoassay, not a monitoring measure of replication or prognosis.
whyWrongByChoice.D: p24 antigen detection is part of the initial screen for diagnosis, not a quantitative prognostic marker.

questions.stem: A 46-year-old man with untreated HIV comes for follow-up. He feels well and has no history of opportunistic infections or malignancy. His CD4+ T cell count is 180/uL. Which of the following best classifies his infection?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Acute phase

choices.label: B
choices.text: Clinical latency

choices.label: C
choices.text: HIV Stage 1

choices.label: D
choices.text: HIV Stage 2

choices.label: E
choices.text: HIV Stage 3

explanation.summary: A CD4+ count below 200/uL is HIV Stage 3, also known as AIDS, even without an AIDS-defining illness.
explanation.whyCorrect: HIV is staged by CD4+ T cell count: Stage 1 is 500 or more cells/uL, Stage 2 is 200-499, and Stage 3 (AIDS) is below 200. In people aged 6 years or older, a CD4 count under 200/uL alone meets the definition of AIDS.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The acute phase is the first 0-12 weeks after infection, often with a normal CD4 count.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Feeling well does not override the CD4 criterion; a count under 200/uL defines AIDS.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Stage 1 requires a CD4+ count of at least 500/uL.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Stage 2 covers CD4+ counts of 200-499/uL; his count is below 200.

questions.stem: A 40-year-old woman undergoes routine HIV screening at an annual visit. Her HIV-1/2 antigen/antibody immunoassay is reactive. She is asymptomatic. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step to establish the diagnosis?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Begin ART now without any confirmatory testing

choices.label: B
choices.text: CD4+ T cell count to confirm the infection is present

choices.label: C
choices.text: HIV-1/HIV-2 antibody-differentiation immunoassay

choices.label: D
choices.text: Rapid IgG-only antibody test as an independent recheck

choices.label: E
choices.text: Repeat the same antigen/antibody immunoassay in 6 months

explanation.summary: A reactive antigen/antibody screen is confirmed with an antibody-differentiation immunoassay or NAAT.
explanation.whyCorrect: In the standard HIV testing algorithm, the first test is an HIV-1/2 antigen/antibody immunoassay detecting p24 antigen plus HIV-specific IgM and IgG. If it is positive, an antibody-differentiation immunoassay or NAAT confirms the diagnosis.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Treatment decisions follow a confirmed diagnosis; the algorithm requires confirmation first.
whyWrongByChoice.B: CD4 count gauges immune compromise but does not confirm HIV infection.
whyWrongByChoice.D: An IgG-only antibody test is not the confirmatory step in the algorithm.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Waiting 6 months delays diagnosis; a reactive screen should go straight to confirmatory testing.

questions.stem: A term male infant is seen at 16 days of life. His mother has HIV and was on antiretroviral therapy during pregnancy. The pediatrician wants to determine whether the infant is infected. Which of the following is the most appropriate test?

choices.label: A
choices.text: HIV nucleic acid test (NAT)

choices.label: B
choices.text: HIV-1/2 antibody-differentiation immunoassay

choices.label: C
choices.text: HIV-1/2 antigen/antibody immunoassay

choices.label: D
choices.text: Infant CD4+ T cell count

choices.label: E
choices.text: Maternal viral load at delivery

explanation.summary: Infants born to people with HIV are tested by NAT (at 14-21 days, 1-2 months, and 4-6 months), not by antibody-based screens.
explanation.whyCorrect: Maternal IgG crosses the placenta and causes false-positive antigen/antibody screens in the newborn, so the standard algorithm is not used. All babies born to people with HIV should be tested with NAT at 14 to 21 days of life, at 1 to 2 months, and again at 4 to 6 months.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Antibody-based differentiation also detects maternal IgG and cannot establish infant infection.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Transplacental maternal IgG can make this screen falsely positive in the newborn.
whyWrongByChoice.D: CD4 count does not diagnose HIV infection.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Maternal viral load informs transmission risk but does not diagnose infection in the infant.

questions.stem: A 29-year-old woman presents with 4 days of fever, pharyngitis, diffuse rash, and cervical and axillary lymphadenopathy. Three weeks ago a condom broke during intercourse with a partner who has HIV and does not take treatment. An HIV-1/2 antigen/antibody immunoassay is nonreactive. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Order a CD4+ T cell count to guide staging

choices.label: B
choices.text: Order a nucleic acid amplification test (NAAT)

choices.label: C
choices.text: Order an antibody-differentiation immunoassay

choices.label: D
choices.text: Reassure her that HIV infection has been ruled out

choices.label: E
choices.text: Repeat only the immunoassay in 3 months

explanation.summary: A negative initial screen does not rule out HIV in a patient with acute retroviral syndrome and recent high-risk exposure; test by NAAT.
explanation.whyCorrect: One exception to the standard algorithm: if a patient has symptoms of acute retroviral syndrome and a recent high-risk exposure but a negative initial screen, HIV should not be ruled out. Instead, test by NAAT, which detects viral nucleic acid during the high-viremia acute phase.

whyWrongByChoice.A: CD4 count does not diagnose infection and may remain normal in the acute phase.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The differentiation assay confirms a reactive screen; it is not the next step after a negative screen with high suspicion.
whyWrongByChoice.D: HIV must not be ruled out on a negative screen when acute retroviral syndrome follows a high-risk exposure.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Waiting months delays diagnosis of a symptomatic acute infection that NAAT can detect now.

questions.stem: A 33-year-old man is newly diagnosed with HIV and has no evidence of drug resistance. He is ready to start treatment. Which of the following describes a common initial antiretroviral regimen?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A fusion inhibitor combined with one NNRTI

choices.label: B
choices.text: A single NRTI given as monotherapy

choices.label: C
choices.text: An INSTI combined with two NRTIs

choices.label: D
choices.text: Ritonavir combined with cobicistat alone

choices.label: E
choices.text: Two protease inhibitors without any booster

explanation.summary: Common initial ART regimens pair an integrase strand transfer inhibitor with two NRTIs.
explanation.whyCorrect: Because HIV mutates rapidly, treatment combines drugs from more than one class. Common initial regimens use an INSTI plus two NRTIs, such as bictegravir/tenofovir alafenamide/emtricitabine or dolutegravir plus tenofovir with emtricitabine or lamivudine.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Fusion inhibitors such as enfuvirtide are not routine first-line ART.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Monotherapy invites resistance in a rapidly mutating virus; ART combines drug classes.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Ritonavir and cobicistat are pharmacokinetic boosters that inhibit CYP450, not a stand-alone regimen.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Two protease inhibitors from a single class are not the described initial regimen.

questions.stem: A 31-year-old nurse sustains a deep needlestick injury while drawing blood from a patient with HIV who has a detectable viral load. She presents to occupational health 20 hours later. Her baseline HIV test is sent. Which of the following is the most appropriate management?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Start daily oral PrEP and continue indefinitely

choices.label: B
choices.text: Start post-exposure prophylaxis now for 28 days

choices.label: C
choices.text: Start post-exposure prophylaxis now for 7 days

choices.label: D
choices.text: Start post-exposure prophylaxis only if fever develops

choices.label: E
choices.text: Wait for her baseline result, then decide in 1 week

explanation.summary: PEP is started as soon as possible (ideally within 24 h, no later than 72 h) and taken for 28 days.
explanation.whyCorrect: Post-exposure prophylaxis is antiretroviral medication given after a possible exposure such as a needlestick injury. It should be started as soon as possible, ideally within 24 hours and no later than 72 hours, and is taken for 28 days, for example bictegravir/emtricitabine/tenofovir alafenamide.

whyWrongByChoice.A: PrEP is taken before possible exposure by a person without HIV; this is a post-exposure situation.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The PEP course is 28 days, not 7.
whyWrongByChoice.D: PEP is started promptly after exposure, not held until symptoms appear.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Waiting a week would pass the 72-hour window for starting PEP.

questions.stem: A 30-year-old woman with HIV arrives in labor with an unknown current viral load. She receives an intravenous antiretroviral during delivery, and her newborn is started on the same drug orally as prophylaxis. Which adverse effect of this drug most requires monitoring in the infant?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Anemia and neutropenia on the complete blood count

choices.label: B
choices.text: Flare of hepatitis B virus when the drug is stopped

choices.label: C
choices.text: Hyperlipidemia and insulin resistance on metabolic labs

choices.label: D
choices.text: Painful erythematous nodules at injection sites

choices.label: E
choices.text: Reduced renal function and low bone mineral density

explanation.summary: Zidovudine, used intrapartum IV and for neonatal prophylaxis, causes bone marrow suppression requiring CBC monitoring.
explanation.whyCorrect: Zidovudine is the classic drug for preventing perinatal transmission: IV zidovudine may be given intrapartum when maternal viral load is high or unknown, and it is commonly used for neonatal prophylaxis. Its key adverse effect is bone marrow suppression (decreased hematocrit, leukopenia/neutropenia, sometimes thrombocytopenia), so CBC monitoring is needed.

whyWrongByChoice.B: HBV flare on discontinuation is the classic warning for lamivudine in HIV/HBV coinfection.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Hyperlipidemia and insulin resistance are protease inhibitor adverse effects.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Injection-site reactions characterize subcutaneous enfuvirtide.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Effects on kidney function and bone density are associated with tenofovir.

questions.stem: A patient with HIV starts dolutegravir, which prevents insertion of viral DNA into the host cell genome. The enzyme targeted by this drug is encoded by which HIV gene?

choices.label: A
choices.text: env

choices.label: B
choices.text: gag

choices.label: C
choices.text: nef

choices.label: D
choices.text: pol

choices.label: E
choices.text: tat

explanation.summary: pol encodes reverse transcriptase, integrase, and protease, the enzymatic targets of most antiretrovirals.
explanation.whyCorrect: Dolutegravir is an INSTI that inhibits integrase, blocking insertion of viral DNA into the host genome. Integrase, along with reverse transcriptase and protease, is encoded by pol.

whyWrongByChoice.A: env encodes envelope glycoproteins gp120 and gp41.
whyWrongByChoice.B: gag encodes structural proteins p24, p7, and p17, not enzymes.
whyWrongByChoice.C: nef is not among the genes described as encoding the HIV enzymes; integrase comes from pol.
whyWrongByChoice.E: tat is not among the genes described as encoding the HIV enzymes; integrase comes from pol.

questions.stem: A 26-year-old man without HIV takes daily oral tenofovir disoproxil fumarate/emtricitabine as pre-exposure prophylaxis. Which monitoring is most specifically warranted by the tenofovir component?

choices.label: A
choices.text: CBC for anemia and neutropenia

choices.label: B
choices.text: Fasting lipids and glucose

choices.label: C
choices.text: Inspection of injection sites

choices.label: D
choices.text: Renal function and bone mineral density

choices.label: E
choices.text: Screening for neuropsychiatric effects

explanation.summary: Tenofovir can affect kidney function and bone mineral density.
explanation.whyCorrect: Tenofovir is an NRTI used in PrEP (with emtricitabine) and in ART. Beyond the NRTI class risk of mitochondrial toxicity, tenofovir specifically can affect kidney function and bone mineral density.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Bone marrow suppression is the hallmark of zidovudine.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Hyperlipidemia and insulin resistance are protease inhibitor effects.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Injection-site reactions are typical of subcutaneous enfuvirtide, not oral tenofovir.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Neuropsychiatric effects are associated with efavirenz, an NNRTI.

questions.stem: HIV is classified as a retrovirus. Which of the following best describes its virion structure and genome?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Enveloped, circular partially double-stranded DNA

choices.label: B
choices.text: Enveloped, segmented negative-sense RNA

choices.label: C
choices.text: Enveloped, two copies of single-stranded RNA

choices.label: D
choices.text: Nonenveloped, single copy of double-stranded DNA

choices.label: E
choices.text: Nonenveloped, single copy of double-stranded RNA

explanation.summary: Retroviruses such as HIV are enveloped and carry two copies of single-stranded RNA.
explanation.whyCorrect: Retroviruses are enveloped viruses that encode their genetic information as two copies of ssRNA, which reverse transcriptase copies into DNA that integrase inserts into the host genome.

whyWrongByChoice.A: HIV carries RNA in the virion; DNA exists only after reverse transcription in the host cell.
whyWrongByChoice.B: HIV's genome is two copies of ssRNA, not a segmented negative-sense RNA.
whyWrongByChoice.D: HIV is enveloped and has an RNA genome, not a DNA genome.
whyWrongByChoice.E: HIV is enveloped, and its genome is single-stranded, not double-stranded, RNA.

questions.stem: A 45-year-old woman who immigrated from West Africa is found to have HIV. Her antibody-differentiation immunoassay shows antibodies to HIV-2 only. Compared with HIV-1 infection, which of the following is most accurate about her infection?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It cannot progress to AIDS without treatment

choices.label: B
choices.text: It causes the majority of infections worldwide

choices.label: C
choices.text: It infects B cells rather than CD4+ T cells

choices.label: D
choices.text: It is spread only through parenteral exposure

choices.label: E
choices.text: It tends to progress more slowly toward AIDS

explanation.summary: HIV-2 is found mostly in West Africa and progresses more slowly than HIV-1.
explanation.whyCorrect: HIV-1 and HIV-2 cause most infections; HIV-1 is the most common globally, and HIV-2 is mostly found in West Africa. Without treatment, HIV almost always transitions to AIDS, although HIV-2 progresses more slowly than HIV-1.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Untreated HIV almost always progresses to AIDS; HIV-2 simply progresses more slowly.
whyWrongByChoice.B: HIV-1, not HIV-2, is responsible for the majority of infections globally.
whyWrongByChoice.C: HIV targets CD4-bearing cells such as CD4+ T cells, macrophages, and dendritic cells.
whyWrongByChoice.D: HIV is transmitted primarily through sexual contact as well as parenteral and vertical routes.

questions.stem: A 28-year-old woman with HIV delivers a healthy infant. She asks whether her infant could still acquire HIV from her after delivery. Which of the following is a recognized route of transmission from mother to infant after birth?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Bathing the infant together

choices.label: B
choices.text: Breastfeeding the infant

choices.label: C
choices.text: Holding the infant skin to skin

choices.label: D
choices.text: Kissing the infant's face

choices.label: E
choices.text: Sharing eating utensils

explanation.summary: HIV can be transmitted transplacentally, perinatally during delivery, and through breastmilk.
explanation.whyCorrect: HIV is a bloodborne pathogen transmitted via body fluids including blood, semen, pre-seminal fluid, and vaginal secretions. Vertical transmission can occur transplacentally, perinatally during delivery, and through breastmilk, so breastfeeding remains a route after birth.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Bathing together is casual contact, not exposure to infectious blood, genital fluids, or breastmilk.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Skin-to-skin holding is casual contact, not exposure to infectious blood, genital fluids, or breastmilk.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Casual contact such as kissing the skin is not among the body-fluid exposures that transmit HIV.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Casual contact such as sharing utensils is not among the body-fluid exposures that transmit HIV.

questions.stem: A 24-year-old man asks which factors affect his risk of acquiring HIV from a partner who has HIV. Which of the following would most increase his risk per exposure?

choices.label: A
choices.text: His consistent use of condoms with the partner

choices.label: B
choices.text: His having active genital herpes lesions

choices.label: C
choices.text: His having undergone male circumcision

choices.label: D
choices.text: His partner taking ART with suppressed viral load

choices.label: E
choices.text: His taking daily oral pre-exposure prophylaxis

explanation.summary: Concurrent STIs such as active genital herpes increase HIV acquisition risk; condoms, circumcision, ART, and PrEP decrease it.
explanation.whyCorrect: Factors that increase exposure of blood to contaminated fluids raise HIV risk: high viral load, concurrent STIs such as active genital herpes, receptive anal sex, childbirth, limited condom use, and occupational exposures. Genital herpes ulcers disrupt the mucosal barrier.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Consistent condom use decreases the risk of transmission.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Male circumcision is listed as decreasing the risk of transmission.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Antiretroviral treatment of the source partner decreases transmission risk.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Pre-exposure prophylaxis decreases the risk of acquiring HIV.
